\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 30: Lived Days 129–131, Reed 10–12, Tenthday to Secondday, one hundred and twenty-nine through one hundred and thirty-one days old — four months and nine days through four months and eleven days — nobody saying so. On Day 129 read the Account-day figure over the crowd at the Cross as a chart closed over a note nobody had opened; Berr’s \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says}, \emph{The levy is called. It is not called by me} and \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, the true subtraction in the locked box, the heard bell beside the told bell, four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself (T015/T041/T047/T077, T078). Went around the missing hand’s place with a look and no number (T098 carried). \textbf{In scene 2, from the basket’s low angle under the Vail loaf shelf, saw short charcoal marks in clusters on the UNDERSIDE of the board, some pressed hard, some faded into the grain, a keeping put where nobody thought to look; did not read, count, copy or show them and did not lay them beside the two gaps above, the fold’s crust, Alda’s tin, Mira’s cords, Orra’s knots, Dessa’s tin or the reed-cutter’s cord. T100 planted and unpaid, held for the far-off day a hand not his lays the district’s records together.} On Day 130 watched Jorra’s grey dust past the bent finger, the men unnamed before first grey, the damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence and the full note withheld from a High Kiln kiln-master (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095); at the hearth heard the sentence about an ear brought \textbf{a third time} to the word that would call the loan and stopped, the breath drawn and unspent, filed as a third interval and not a third payment (T036/T076, T061/T082); below the sill the cold foot stayed the cold to one woman and weather to the yard (T093/T094/T096). On Day 131 at the Weir watched the reed-cutter tie one knot with his teeth and put the cord back unread (\emph{You can ask the cord} / \emph{No more can the Court}), Orra give the ninth of Ilmen with six oars and a man at the stern who never touched them, Mira answer a thin run with her own answer and show the second twist twice beneath the grey with neither knot counted; the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set for an uncalled measure (T099, T024/T059/T025, T090/T080/T083). Three doors down Alda laid her birth-slates before the fold, crossed the flower unknowing, covered it with the date she gave Dessa and said \emph{Warm and breathing} exact and not true, her tin and both records shut (T007/T008/T023/T089). In scene 7 saw Sella’s finger go beneath the board and come away without a word and made no cause of it (T100 carried). Six hearings stood six beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, one crust in the fold with its empty place named by nobody, two shelf gaps in a room that does not touch, the carried fire’s fifth breath unnamed for one hundred and twenty-nine, one hundred and thirty and one hundred and thirty-one days, the count kept edge to edge and spoken by nobody. Old life offstage: no present-tense break, no `**` tag, no power used and no rank change. Nothing joined, named, paid, opened, called or ended; forward.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 31: Lived Days 132–134, Reed 13–15, Thirdday to Fifthday, one hundred and thirty-two through one hundred and thirty-four days old — four months and twelve through fourteen days — nobody saying so. \textbf{Day 132 (Reed 13):} at the Clay Yard and the reed beds watched the yard go around the clean dark line, the new finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with the broken birth-slates and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). Reeds came in armfuls judged by the arm that carried them; a cutter told a girl with a creel \emph{Your arm’ll tell you what went into it, and that’s the whole of what it knows}, and a man who asked what the work would want was given the weather and the river, never a figure (T071/T072, T077). Read the carrying arm as a record in muscle that tells what was carried and not what it cost, exact, complete and worth nothing (T072). Under the Vail roof, from the basket’s low angle, saw Sella reach a finger beneath the loaf shelf where the charcoal tally lies, without looking and without a word; did not read, count, copy or join the strokes, and made no cause of the habit (T100 carried; T060/T086). At the Weir watched the reed-cutter tie one knot with his teeth, bite the end off and put his grey cord back inside his coat, \emph{You can ask the cord} / \emph{No more can the Court} (T099 carried); Orra gave a date where a figure was asked with the word forty unspoken, and Mira’s second twist stayed twice beneath the grey with neither knot counted (T024/T059/T025). \textbf{Day 133 (Reed 14):} before first grey three or four unnamed men went low into the finger’s-width-open back room; Jorra came through with grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger, spoke to the wheel (\emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady}), told a pot \emph{You’ll do}, withheld its full note from a High Kiln kiln-master who would have called it early, and put that finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095). Read the iron again as the bite that holds a vessel whole and can take the hand off a man, filed joined to no kiln. At the hearth heard Tarn bring the sentence about the ear \textbf{a fourth time} to the word that would call the loan and stop there, no figure, no name, the breath drawn and unspent; filed it as a \textbf{fourth interval and not a fourth payment}, refusing to let four stoppings stand up and call themselves a doctrine (T036/T076, T061/T082). The soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the landing for an uncalled measure, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, market sold over him (T090/T080/T083). \textbf{Day 134 (Reed 15):} at the Cross and pot board filed a \textbf{fourth green} at a silent woman’s mouth — clay under her nails, a pale cord-mark on the back of one hand, a cup turned a quarter and set back — as the fourth at a mouth and the fifth shape of the colour counting Berr’s glaze, a colour and not a name, never Fenna in the narration, joined to no ear (T050/T051). Berr wiped his thumb twice, bought eels two marks short, said \emph{A number goes into a slate, not a bundle} and \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and went off with the box locked (T015/T041/T047). Below the sill the child’s foot stayed dark inside three turns of wool, the cold to the woman who wrapped it and weather to the yard; the surgeon’s reading of the extremity going before the core worked perfectly and bought nothing, no silt-leach, cause or cure named (T093/T094/T096). Sella reached beneath the shelf a second time unread. At the close six hearings stood six beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced, four stoppings as objects and not a rule, one crust and no third, two shelf gaps in a room that does not touch, the word forty unspoken, Alda’s six pages and both tins and Dessa’s tin shut, the loan uncalled and the seventh year not given; three counts of river, fire and boards stayed in three places that did not become one. Old life offstage throughout: no present-tense break, no `**` tag, no power used, no rank change. Nothing joined, paid, named, opened, called or ended; forward.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 32: Lived Days 135–137, Reed 16–18, Sixthday to Eighthday, one hundred and thirty-five to one hundred and thirty-seven days old, four months and fifteen to seventeen days, nobody saying so. At the Clay Yard and the reed beds read the carrying arm as a record in muscle that knows what was carried and not what it cost; the woman at the racks who asked what the hands would be paid was answered with the weather and the river, and she shut two fingers out of a fist as she went. Went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates and the missing hand’s place with a look and no number (T098 carried). Under the roof watched Sella’s finger go beneath the loaf shelf where the charcoal tally lies, without looking or a word, and made no cause of it (T100 carried, unread). On Day 136 Jorra’s grey dust, the men unnamed in the back room, the full note withheld from a High Kiln kiln-master and the bent finger in the cold damper ahead of Sella’s sentence (T035/T031/T062); Tarn’s seventh year pressed nearer its end and still held. At the hearth Tarn brought the ear-sentence a FIFTH time to the word that would call the loan and stopped, no figure, no name, breath drawn and unspent; the boy filed a fifth stopping on the interval tray as an object, an interval and not a payment, and would not let five likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine (T036/T076, T061/T082). At the Weir on Day 137 the reed-cutter tied his grey cord low with his teeth, bit the end off and put it back inside his coat with the knots unread (T099); Orra gave the ninth of Ilmen with the boat of six oars and the man at the stern who never touched them and kept the word forty unspoken (T024); Mira answered a thin run with her own answer and showed the second twist twice beneath the grey with neither knot counted, her board beside Orra’s not touching (T059/T025). At the Cross Berr paid two eels short with a slate not a bundle, \emph{your house} never \emph{I}, and the true subtraction stayed in the locked box (T015/T041/T047). Below the sill the child’s dark foot stayed the cold to one woman and weather to the yard, read exactly and worth nothing (T093/T094/T096). At the going of the light he was set on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, the fold righted without a look at his face, the thread frozen, the pot handle two inches beyond his hand; in the small hours he turned out his file complete, exact and worthless, the count one hundred and thirty-seven, unspent and spoken by nobody. No seventh hearing, no sixth sighting, no knot counted, no sale, no tin or box opened, no joining; the old life stayed offstage.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 33: Lived Days 138–140, Reed 19–21, Ninthday to Firstday, one hundred and thirty-eight to one hundred and forty days old, four months and eighteen to twenty days, nobody saying so. \textbf{Day 138 (Reed 19):} the reed month stood in its last tend; last bundles came downriver in armfuls judged by the arm that carried them, a cutter told a girl with a creel to lift her bundle and let her arm say what went into it, \emph{and that’s the whole of what it knows}, and a woman at the racks who asked what the hands would be paid was answered with the weather and the river and shut two fingers out of a fist (T071/T072, T077). Went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates and the empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). Read the carrying arm as a record in muscle that tells what was carried and not what it cost, exact, complete and worth nothing (T061/T082). Under the roof, from the basket’s low angle, watched Sella reach a finger BENEATH the loaf shelf where the charcoal tally lies, without looking or a word, and brought it away; did not read, count or join the strokes or make a cause of the habit (T100 carried, T060/T086). \textbf{Day 139 (Reed 20, second Account-day):} Berr came up short with the red cord folded under his coat and glaze at one mouth-corner, wiped his thumb twice, held a narrow slate unopened, passed a finger over the figure, read \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says}, called the levy and denied it with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}; the true subtraction stayed in the locked box and a figure read aloud was not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047/T077). Filed a \textbf{fifth green} at a silent woman’s mouth across the square --- clay under her nails, a pale line across the back of one hand, a cup turned a quarter and set back --- as the fifth at a mouth and the sixth shape of the colour, a colour and not a name, never Fenna in the narration, joined to no ear (T050/T051 advanced, not paid). The bell went four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, heard beside told (T078); the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing, hand to slate before eyes to stalls (T090/T080/T083). At the stalls Berr paid two marks short for eels and went up the road believing he had done a kindness; below the sill the child’s dark foot stayed the cold to one woman and weather to the yard, read exactly and worth nothing (T093/T094/T096). At the hearth Tarn brought the ear-sentence a \textbf{SIXTH} time to the word that would call the loan and stopped, no figure, no name, breath drawn and unspent; the boy filed a sixth stopping on the interval tray as an object and not a rule, an interval and not a payment, and would not let six likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine (T036/T076, T061/T082). \textbf{Day 140 (Reed 21):} before first grey three or four unnamed men went low into the finger’s-width-open back room; Jorra came through with fine grey slate dust, spoke to the wheel first, withheld a pot’s full note from a High Kiln kiln-master and put his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence (T035/T031/T062); Tarn’s seventh year pressed nearer its end and still held, his stroke going on past the bright patch without the half-check. At the Weir the reed-cutter turned his grey cord so the knots stood, tied one low with his teeth, bit the end off and put it back inside his coat unread (T099); Orra gave a date where a figure was asked and kept the word forty unspoken (T024); Mira answered a thin run with her own answer and showed the second twist twice beneath the grey with neither knot counted, her board beside Orra’s not touching (T059/T025). Up the clay road at dusk Sella carried him around a pan set out to dry and an iced trough and set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, fold righted without a look at his face, thread frozen, pot handle two inches beyond his hand; in the small hours he turned out his file complete, exact and worthless, six hearings with no seventh, six stoppings with no payer, five greens as colours, and the count one hundred and forty unspent and spoken by nobody. No seventh hearing, no sixth sighting, no knot counted, no name, cause or body for the missing hand, no third gap, no sale, no tin or box opened, no joining; the old life stayed offstage throughout. Forward, not closed.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 34: Lived Days 141–143, Reed 22–24, Secondday to Fourthday, one hundred and forty-one, forty-two and forty-three days old, four months and twenty-one to twenty-three days, nobody saying so. \textbf{Day 141:} at the Clay Yard and reed beds the last bundles came up judged by the arm that carried them, a cutter told a girl with a creel her arm knew what went into a bundle and that was the whole of it, and a woman asking what the hands would be paid was answered with the weather and the river and shut two fingers out of a fist; the yard went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the broken birth-slates and the place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T098 carried); a reed-cutter’s grey cord went past along the boards straightened and turned where no slate lay, its knots unread (T099 carried). Under the roof a neighbour reached past the bare board with her hand before her eyes and named the old shelf-gap and the empty place at his ear under one appetite in a single breath, a further shaping of T097 filed on a place of its own, advanced and not paid, no third gap and no joining; Sella sent her to the pot with the house has said it and reached a finger BENEATH the loaf shelf where the charcoal lies without looking or a word, bringing it away (T100 carried, unread). Read the carrying arm as a record in muscle that tells what was carried and not what it cost, exact, complete and worth nothing. \textbf{Day 142:} before first grey men with collars high went low into the room off the wheel-shed and Sella gave them no name and did not say the room was cold; Jorra came through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent finger, spoke to the wheel, told a pot it would do, knew its full note three turns ahead and withheld it from a High Kiln kiln-master, and put that finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, the double bite filed as an object joined to no kiln with no third telling of the shut room (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095). Tarn’s seventh year pressed nearer its end than ever, knife at the edge of its sill, six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it, his stroke going on over the flagstones past the bright patch without the half-check. At the Cross Berr Clay read one in twelve, called the levy and denied it with your house, never I, paid two marks short for two pair of eels which the stall-keeper put in her palm uncounted, and went up the road with the true subtraction locked in the box believing he had done a kindness (T015/T041/T047/T077); below the bridge the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set for a measure nobody called (T090/T080). At the hearth Tarn told the kindling Six counted. The next I don’t count and brought the ear-sentence a SEVENTH time, on Reed 23 after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 and 20, all the way to the word that would call the loan, stopping there with no figure and no name and drawing the breath he did not spend; the boy filed the seventh stopping on the interval tray beside six as an interval and not a seventh payment, refusing to let seven likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine because no payer had been named to any (T036/T076, T061/T082). \textbf{Day 143:} downriver at the Weir a reed-cutter set his bundle on the flat blessing stone, straightened his grey thumb-oiled cord, turned it so the knots stood, tied one low with his teeth, bit the end off and put it back inside his coat, telling a woman who could not read it You can ask the cord and No more can the Court, no knot counted (T099 carried); Orra pulled one knot down and gave the ninth of Ilmen, the collector’s boat with six oars and the man at the stern who never touched them, the forty-first double turn legible and the word forty unspoken (T024); Mira answered a thin run with Ask the river, flicked eel-bones while deciding whether to lie, and when a buyer named a figure put her thumb under her apron to the grey cord with a second twist twice beneath it, never carried upriver to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted, her board beside Orra’s and not touching (T059/T025). Three private records stood within a dozen paces of the basket and none was enterable; below the sill the child’s foot stayed dark in three turns of wool, the cold to the woman who wrapped it and weather to the yard, the reading of the extremity going before the core working perfectly and buying nothing (T093/T094/T096). The clerk stayed set; in the afternoon the last bundles stood grey in the ruts uncounted with the third Account-day six days off, the yard going around its two lines, the rack space and the empty place with a look and no number, and Sella, moving her lips along the row with its two unnamed gaps, reached a finger beneath the board without looking or a word (T100 carried). At the going of the light she carried him up around the pan and iced trough, set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread frozen, told the fire it was the thaw and said The house will keep it, and in the small hours he turned out his file as a man lays instruments on a towel and found every object in its place and nothing laid across anything else — six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, seven stoppings on the tray with no payer named to any, the damper’s double bite, the two shut-room tellings with no third, the told bell beside the heard, the fifth green a colour and not a name — one hundred and forty-three exact and unspent and the loan uncalled with the seventh year one tend from its end, wanting the crust two inches from his ear and his number spoken by somebody who would know what a number was and getting neither, his hand going up an inch toward the note of water over water and coming down against the fold. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no power moved, no rank change and no experiment; nothing joined, paid, named, opened, called, spent or ended. Forward, not closed.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 35: Lived Days 144–146, Reed 25–27, one hundred and forty-four to one hundred and forty-six days old, carried at the half-pace from every open slate. On Day 144 read the last bundles of reed as a record in muscle, judged by the arm that carried them and never by a figure; a girl with a creel was told her arm knew what went into a bundle and that was the whole of it, and a man who asked what the hands would be paid was answered with the weather and the river. The yard went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates and the empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T098 carried). Saw Sella’s finger go beneath the loaf shelf and come away without a look or a word, and read nothing of the charcoal under the board (T100 carried). On Day 145 watched Jorra come through with grey slate dust past the bent finger, speak to the wheel and a pot, withhold the full note from a High Kiln kiln-master and put that finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence; at the Weir and below the sill kept Mira’s grey cord with its second twist, Orra’s legible unnamed double turn, the reed-cutter’s cord and the child’s dark foot on places that do not touch (T099, T024/T059/T025, T093/T094/T096 carried). At the going of the light heard Tarn bring the ear-sentence an \textbf{eighth} time, after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20 and 23, to the word that would call the loan and stop there with no figure and no name, drawing the breath he did not spend and saying \emph{Yes, house} to the fire; filed the eighth stopping on the interval tray beside seven as an interval and not a payment, refusing to let eight likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine (T036/T076, T061/T082). On Day 146 watched Alda lay her birth-slates before the fold three doors down, cross the flower unknowing, cover it with \emph{Stone seven. The account went up on the eighth, before the paper went out}, say \emph{Warm and breathing} exact and not true, touch her tin unopened and leave six pages turned toward a floorboard with both tins shut (T007/T008/T023/T089, not paid again). At the going of the light was set on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, the fold put right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face, the thread of drool left frozen and unwiped, the pot handle two inches beyond his reaching hand; in the small hours turned out the file complete, exact and worthless with six hearings beside and never among and no seventh, eight stoppings with no payer named to any, five greens as colours, and the river’s note, the fire’s missing fifth pull and the boards’ knot still three counts in three places that do not become one, and his hand went up an inch toward the water and came down with one hundred and forty-six exact and unspent. The old life stayed offstage: no present-tense break, no `**` tag, no departure from his eyes. No power moved, no rank change, no opening, no ending.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 36: Lived Days 147–149, Reed 28–30, Eighthday to Tenthday, one hundred and forty-seven through one hundred and forty-nine days old — four months and twenty-seven to twenty-nine days — nobody saying so. On Day 147 the last bundles came out of the reed beds judged by the arm that carried them; a cutter told a girl with a creel that her arm knew what went into a bundle and that was the whole of it, and a man who asked what the hands would be paid was answered with the weather and the river, never a figure (T071/T072, T077). Went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the broken birth-slates and the empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried); the reed-cutter’s grey cord went past along the boards straightened and turned where no slate lay, tied low with teeth and put back inside his coat with its knots unread (T099 carried). Under the roof, from the basket’s low angle, watched Sella reach a finger BENEATH the loaf shelf where the charcoal tally lies, without looking and without a word, and read nothing of the marks (T100 carried, unread). On Day 148 watched the men unnamed go low into the back room before first grey, Jorra’s fine grey slate dust past the bent finger, the full note known before a High Kiln kiln-master and withheld, and the bent finger in the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence (T035/T031/T062); at the Weir kept the reed-cutter’s cord, Orra’s legible unnamed double turn with the word forty unspoken, Mira’s second twist beneath the grey, the clerk’s inward slate and the child’s dark foot on five places that do not touch (T099, T024/T059/T025, T090/T080, T093/T094/T096). At the going of the light heard Tarn tell the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and bring the ear-sentence a \textbf{ninth} time — after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23 and 26 — to the word that would call the loan and stop there with no figure and no name, drawing the breath he did not spend; filed the ninth stopping on the interval tray beside eight as an interval and not a payment, and would not let nine likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and no payer had been named to any of the nine (T036/T076, T061/T082). On Day 149, the third Account-day and last market of Reed, watched Berr wipe his thumb twice, hold a narrow slate unopened, read \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says}, call the levy and deny it with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, pay two marks short for eels into an uncounted palm and go off up the clay road with the box locked and the true subtraction inside — a figure read aloud that was not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047/T077); the bell went four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, heard beside told (T078), and the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called (T090/T080). Filed a \textbf{sixth} green at a silent woman’s mouth at the pot board and a \textbf{sixth} silent glimpse of the foundling at the market’s edge — cast-offs worn like a uniform, silt dried pale in his wrists, a gap where a front tooth had been, a green sliver on a string at his throat, his head a half-beat late toward a set-down pot and stopping in the middle of the turn, no loaf, no slate and no sale — as a colour and a shape on places of their own, never Fenna in the narration and the foundling unnamed and given no dialogue (T050/T051, T033/T034). At the going of the light Sella set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread of drool frozen, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and went to her own bed; in the small hours his file held six hearings and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, nine stoppings with no payer named, a sixth colour and a sixth shape, one stiff crust with its empty place, and the loan uncalled as the count crossed into Smoke exact and unspent. Nothing joined, paid, named, opened, called or ended.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 37: Lived Days 150–152, Tallow 1–3, Firstday to Thirdday, one hundred and fifty to one hundred and fifty-two days old --- five months to five months and two days --- nobody saying so. On Day 150, at the first firing of the month, watched Sella Vail put her hand to the widow’s mark before the kiln mouth, hold it one breath and let go, and tip the carried coal under the back of a broken pot, the fire answering four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been with its payer unnamed for a hundred and fifty days (T058/T079, T088); read the opening as a theatre he could not enter and the damper as one iron with two bites joined to no kiln (T062). The pan set out to dry through Reed was gone with no scrape, crumb, print, chip or word, and he held its empty place on a place of its own (T097, T060/T086). The yard went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the broken birth-slates under the lowest rack and the empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried); men unnamed went low into the finger’s-width-open back room with no third telling of the shut counting room (T035/T031, T065/T095); Jorra’s full note was withheld from a High Kiln kiln-master on the near-full tray (T061/T082), and Tarn’s stroke went over the bright patch without the half-check with the loan uncalled (T036/T076). On Day 151 at the Weir, the last reed work a direction answered with a direction, watched the reed-cutter’s cord, Orra’s date with the six-oared boat, Mira’s second twist, the clerk’s inward slate and the child’s dark foot stand within a dozen paces and none be entered (T099, T024/T059/T025, T090/T080, T093/T094/T096), and saw Sella’s finger go beneath the loaf shelf where the charcoal tally lies without looking or a word (T100 carried, unread). On Day 152 saw Jorra’s dust, the withheld note and the damper’s double bite again, and heard Tarn tell the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and bring the ear-sentence up as on the nine earlier days, but on this day it stopped short of the threshold, no tenth stopping stood up and the loan stayed uncalled (T036/T076). Six hearings stayed six with no seventh and nine stoppings stayed nine objects on the widened tray with no payer named to any (T061/T082). One hundred and fifty, one hundred and fifty-one and one hundred and fifty-two stood exact, complete and unspent, and his hand went up an inch toward the note of water over water and came down against the fold each night.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 38: Lived Days 153–159, Tallow 4–10, Fourthday to Tenthday, one hundred and fifty-three through one hundred and fifty-nine days old — five months and three days to five months and nine days — nobody saying so. Seven dated days, the kiln breathing in fours with a gap behind the wall, the carried fire answering four low pulls with the fifth missing under the floor and the river’s note through the finger’s-width door, three counts in three places that did not become one (T088, T071/T072). Read the opening as a theatre he could not enter and the damper as one iron with two bites joined to no kiln (T062); went around the clean dark line, the thaw, the broken birth-slates and the hand’s empty place with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). On Day 154 Jorra’s grey dust, the withheld full note and the finger in the damper; Tarn’s stroke went on over the flagstones without the half-check, nine stoppings stayed nine, no collector came and the loan stayed uncalled (T035/T031, T061/T082, T036/T076). At the Weir on Day 155 the last reed work was a direction, the carrying arm knew weight and not cost, Orra gave the ninth of Ilmen where a figure was asked, Mira’s second twist stayed twice beneath the creel with neither knot counted and the reed-cutter’s cord went along the boards unread (T077, T024/T059/T025, T099); the child’s foot stayed dark in three turns of wool and the surgeon’s reading bought nothing (T093/T094/T096). On Day 156 a man in Mud End taken quiet in his sleep was spoken of sideways and called merciful, no lesson made and no figure put to him. On Day 157 Sella’s finger went beneath the loaf shelf’s front edge where the charcoal lies, without looking, and he saw the hand go under and come back and nothing of the marks (T100 carried, unread); no third gap and no fourth likeness. On Day 158 Hessa Rale of Slate Row came through with Berr’s narrow slate held edge-on, hand to slate before eye to yard — an eighth record-first hand filed on a place of its own and joined to none (T080, advanced and not paid) — while a number went from a fist up the clay road and arrived nowhere. On Day 159 Berr read one in twelve at the Cross, denied the levy with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and went off with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness; bell four, four and a gap, heard beside told (T015/T041/T047, T078). In the small hours the file was exact and worthless, one hundred and fifty-nine exact, complete and unspent, the fire missing its fifth and the charcoal waiting for a hand that is not his and a day that has not come. Old life offstage: no remembered line, no present-tense break. Nothing joined, paid, named or ended.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 39: Lived Days 160–162, Tallow 11–13, Firstday to Thirdday, one hundred and sixty to one hundred and sixty-two days old — five months and ten days to five months and twelve days — nobody saying so. New numbered days held exact and unspent (T071/T072); carried fire’s payer unnamed through 162, kiln in fours with a gap and the fifth missing under the floor (T088); instruction to wool, fire, pot, broom and running water, never the basket, \emph{the house}, half-pace, widow’s mark untouched at a morning, a shelf, a well, a rack, a road, a bed and a dusk, pot handle two inches beyond the hand, rooms that do not touch (T058/T079). Yard went around clean dark line, thaw, broken birth-slates and the hand’s empty place with a look and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). On Day 160 finger beneath the shelf’s front edge where the charcoal lies, without looking or a word, brought away unread (T100); a wet-pot neighbour’s cost sent to the pot without a figure (T077). On Day 161 first fraction under the roof: Jorra’s bent finger held back from the cold damper until Sella finished \emph{It wants feeding}, then moved a hair’s breadth and left it standing; filed on a place of its own as a change held and unspoken, not reconciliation, hearing or payment, no payer named, apart from Tarn’s unchecking stroke and the nine stoppings (T062/T035/T031, T061/T082); men unnamed before first grey, grey dust ground small as meal, full note known and withheld from a High Kiln kiln-master who said a pot singing early sings itself out early, the knowing on the near-full tray and not among the hearings (T035/T031). Tarn’s stroke over the flagstones without the half-check, ear-sentence to the teeth and no further, six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, Seed 16 breath unspent, loan uncalled, no tenth (T036/T076). On Day 162 at the Weir reeds counted in the carrying arm, cost answered with river and weather, Orra’s date where a figure was asked and her thumb’s return undecided, Mira’s \emph{Ask the river} and second twist twice beneath the creel with neither knot counted, the reed-cutter’s cord tied once with teeth and hidden, the soft-cuffed clerk set for an uncalled measure, a girl with a creel taking the out-of-line landing sideways, the child’s dark foot in three turns of wool with a perfect reading worth nothing (T077, T024/T059/T025, T099, T090/T080, T093/T094/T096). Crust stiff two inches from his ear with its gap unnamed and no third, two shelf gaps, pan’s gone place on its own tray (T060/T086/T097). Old life offstage: no remembered line, no Chicago break.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 40: Lived Days 163–169, Tallow 14–20, Fourthday to Tenthday, one hundred and sixty-three through one hundred and sixty-nine days old — five months and thirteen days to five months and nineteen days — nobody saying so. Seven dated days at the passage cap; the kiln brought up for the third working week, breathing in fours with a gap behind the wall, the carried fire answering four low pulls with the fifth missing under the floor and its payer unnamed for a hundred and sixty-three through a hundred and sixty-nine days, the river’s note through the finger’s-width door — three counts in three places that did not become one (T088, T071/T072). Read the firing as an operating theatre he could not enter, heat kept and counted behind a screen, a gate with two bites and a cost paid by a man whose name was not spoken (T062). Instruction to wool, fire, pot, broom and running water, never the basket; \emph{the house}; half-pace; widow’s mark untouched at a morning, a shelf, a hearth, a dusk, a road and a square; pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand; two rooms that do not touch (T058/T079). Yard went around the clean dark line, the thaw, the rack space, the broken birth-slates and the empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). On Day 164 Jorra’s dust ground small as meal, the full note known before a High Kiln kiln-master and withheld, no pot lost, and his bent finger waiting at the damper until Sella’s sentence finished, the Day 161 fraction held and unspoken (T035/T031, T061/T082, T062). On Day 165 Tarn told the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, nine stoppings still nine objects with no tenth, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled (T036/T076); a kiln-hand’s sideways word about the man in Mud End was called merciful and made into no lesson. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change:} on Day 166, under the Vail roof at the loaf shelf, Sella’s finger went BENEATH the front edge where the charcoal tally lies and held for the length of one of the breaths she counts before coming away, without looking, reading, copying, giving a word or going back that night; the boy filed the held beat on a place of its own as a change held and unspoken, no payer named, kept from standing up with the Day 161 fraction and the older intervals into a rule, for a rule is an account that has found a payer (T100 carried and advanced, not paid; T061/T082). No third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause; the pan’s gone place, the two shelf gaps, the fold’s crust and its gap and the field’s empty place stayed on their own trays (T060/T086/T097). On Day 167 downriver at the Weir the reed-cutter tied one knot with his teeth and hid his cord, saying \emph{You can ask the cord} and \emph{No more can the Court} (T099); Orra gave the ninth of Ilmen where a figure was asked and her thumb’s return was undecided (T024/T059/T025); Mira answered a buyer’s figure with \emph{Two marks the pair and two short} and did not look into the basket (T059/T025); the child’s foot stayed dark in three turns of wool and the perfect reading bought nothing at two paces (T093/T094/T096); the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set for an uncalled measure (T090/T080). On Day 168 the district’s arithmetic gathered in fists, mouths, loaves and knots without agreeing. On Day 169, the second Account-day and market-day, Berr read \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says}, denied the levy with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and sent a man with a number in his fist to a slate at the watch; the figure read was not the figure paid and the true subtraction went back up the clay road in the locked box (T015/T041/T047, T077); bell four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, heard beside told (T078); Hessa Rale went up the clay road with Berr’s narrow slate edge-on, hand to slate before eye to crowd, a runner and not a reader, joined to no other keeping (T080 advanced, not paid). In the small hours the file was exact and worthless: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, nine stoppings with no payer named and no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the Day 161 fraction and the Day 166 held beat on separate places, two shut-room tellings with no third, told bell beside heard. One hundred and sixty-nine stood exact, complete and unspent; he had stopped expecting to be told what the number counts, which is not the same as not wanting it, and cold arrived at cheek, temple and wrist. Old life offstage: no remembered line, no present-tense Chicago break, no departure from his eyes.

\end{itemize}
}

\CRcharacter*{Jorra Vail}{the wheel-keeper who has never said which side he is on}{build/art/characters/jorra-vail.png}{\CRfield{Also called}{Jorra, Jorra of the Vail, the wheel-keeper}\CRfield{Role}{family}\CRfield{Born}{Y.H. 796, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath}\CRfield{Kind}{human (Grathic)}\CRfield{Origin}{Low Kiln, Sill, Grath; House Vail}\CRfield{Allegiance}{House Vail kiln-house; Kiln-Masters of Sill; quietly courted by the Broken Slates}\CRfield{Status}{alive — \emph{he’s not Vail} still sealed and the promise to the slate-burners still ungiven at the close of Day 169, Tallow 20; on Day 164 came through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal on both forearms, told a pot \emph{You’ll do}, withheld its full note from a High Kiln kiln-master who said a pot singing early would sing itself out early, no pot lost, and for the second time held his bent finger at the cold damper until Sella’s instruction had finished, the fraction held and unspoken}\CRfield{First seen}{Chapter 2}}{\CRsheetheading{Appearance}
Sixteen and built like a gate hinge: tall for a clay boy, narrow, with slip dried to the colour of old bone up both forearms and a permanent bend in his left little finger from a splinter off the wheel when he was eleven. He cuts his hair short so Ash cannot nest in it, which is a thing the district notices and he never explains. His eyes do not finish sentences; they go to the door, to the fire, to the wheel, and come back without reporting. He smells of damp clay, tallow and the sweetish edge of lead glaze carried up from High Kiln on a bad wind. The thing people notice first is his hands, which are the hands of a thrower and have been working since he was nine. The thing they notice last is that he never looks at Sella when she speaks to him, though he obeys her instantly.

\CRsheetheading{Voice \& Manner}
Short, flat, declarative. He asks almost no questions, and when he does it is the tool rather than the clay: \emph{Is it dry? Did you fire it? Who wrote it?} He speaks to the wheel and to the pots as other men speak to animals, and only then to people. When he is angry he gets quieter, the way Sella does, and the household has learned to read the lowering of his voice as a weather signal. He never says \emph{with} or \emph{against} when \emph{I haven’t said} will do.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item “The wheel doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady.”

\item “You want me to say it. I’m not saying it.”

\item “Sella. Don’t feed him from your own dish. He’s not Vail.”

\item “A slate burns in four minutes. Four. I’ve timed it.”

\item “I didn’t say I was with them. I said I wasn’t against them. That’s different. In this district it isn’t, but it’s what I said.”

\item “He’s not Vail.” --- said in the kiln-house at first light, refused an answer, and sealed by the boy’s arrival.

\item “You’ll do.” --- to the pot on the wheel, in a voice with no welcome in it and no unkindness either.

\item “It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady.” --- to the wheel before anyone, said again on Day 140 of a pot he told \emph{You’ll do} while keeping its full note from a High Kiln kiln-master who said it was singing before its time.

\end{itemize}

\CRsheetheading{History}
He is the son of Garl and Sella Vail, and he took the wheel at thirteen when Garl died in the Long Cold and did not come back and nobody came to draw him. The wheel had been Garl’s for twenty years and the seat was worn hollow; Jorra has spent three years trying to fill that hollow with his own weight. He has thrown pots since he was nine, fired them since eleven, and knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves his hands, though he will not say so in front of the kiln-masters, who would call it early and make something of it. His house has remembered the Ash Rising since Y.H. 668, when children were taken and the rising was put down by a man with a list; the memory is kept not in stories but in the way certain doors are never closed and certain names are never entered. Since he was fourteen men from the Broken Slates have come into the back room of the kiln-house and spoken in low voices. He has listened to all of them and told none of them yes.

He watched Enna, his sister, die of the second chill at four, and has never forgiven the fire for being warm while she cooled. He watched his father die and was sent to find a collector and could not cross the ford, and has never asked whether he was sent too late or whether he was sent at all. When Corin arrived he said one sentence — \emph{He’s not Vail} — and has said nothing about it since, which in that house is a form of argument.

\CRsheetheading{Wounds \& Fears}
A father who went uncollected, a sister who went cold in a warm room, and a wheel he was given before he was ready. He fears Sella will die with something unsaid and leave him holding the house and the lie together. He fears the Broken Slates will decide for him what he is, because he has not decided and the longer he waits the more their decision looks like his own. He fears the boy most of all, because the boy hears things. His contradiction: he is the most careful keeper of the Vail fire in four generations and he is quietly helping the people who want to burn every slate in Sill. He has never once thought these two facts cannot live in the same man.

\CRsheetheading{Desires}
He wants the wheel to stay in the house and the fire to hold and nobody to write the boy down as Vail without asking him first. He thinks he wants Sella to say that he has done well with the wheel. What he needs is to learn that burning a slate does not return a person to you, and that the anger he has been nursing for three years is not his alone — it has been lent to him by men who intend to collect on it.

\CRsheetheading{Bonds}
\textbf{Sella Vail} — his mother. He believes she took Corin in to replace Enna and to keep the house’s standing after Garl died. She has never contradicted him. Every obedience he gives her is therefore double: it is love and it is a correction neither of them will make. \emph{Ch 2:} she announced the taking and he answered \emph{he’s not Vail}; she got quieter and gave him no answer at all. He went on working, did not look at her, and shifted the damper before she had finished telling him to.

\textbf{Corin} — the foundling. Jorra was the first in the house to notice that the boy turns his head toward a pot before anyone taps it, and that he does it to hear the note, not the noise. He has told nobody. He resents the boy for being given a bed in the house while the clay-bound hand sleeps in the loft, and he cannot stop watching him. \emph{Ch 2:} the foundling arrived under the roof and nobody wrote him as Vail, which is what Jorra wanted and what he cannot bear. He spoke to the wheel, to the pots and once to Tarn about a rasp out of its place, and never addressed the boy.

\textbf{Alda Reed} — attended Enna’s death and Corin’s birth, and has never met Jorra’s eye for longer than a moment. He knows she wrote something down the night Enna died and has never asked to see it, because asking would make it a thing between them.

\textbf{Tarn} — the Vail’s clay-bound hand. Jorra treats him as a brother when the wheel needs him and as a servant when it does not. Tarn has decided to hate him for it and keeps failing, because Jorra once sat up all night with him through a fever and has never mentioned it. \emph{Ch 2:} Tarn was given the loft while the foundling was given the bed, and said so in one sentence to Sella. Jorra said nothing; he has never defended the household’s arithmetic and never contests it.

\textbf{Berr Clay, the Thane of Clay} — Jorra threw a stone at his door in Y.H. 810 and denied it. The Thane suspects the boy is with the Broken Slates and lets him be, which Jorra finds more frightening than being watched.

\textbf{Ch 4.} Sella’s hand went to the mark before the kiln and not at the bank; he shifted the damper before she had finished and again at dusk, and did not take up her silence about the back room. The boy was at the edge of his notice as a thing that hears: he spoke to the pots and not to him, and came in from the back room with slate dust worked into his forearms --- grey and fine, not slip --- and said \emph{the back room’s cold} to nobody. He wanted the boy outside the name Vail and the hollow seat his, and did not say either.

\textbf{Ch 5.} The wheel took the house into its rhythm again with slip dried to old bone up both forearms and no slate dust on Stone 13 or Stone 15; the boy noticed the absence and could not ask which it meant. He told a pot \emph{you’ll do}, told the wheel it did not care whose hands were on it, and shifted the damper before Sella had finished telling him the fire was low. He did not say the back room was cold. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed as it had been on the hour it was spoken, and the foundling went on being carried under the roof without a Vail name, which is what Jorra wanted and what he could not bear.

\textbf{Ch 6.} On all five days he came in from the shed with bone-coloured slip dried to old bone up both forearms and the bent little finger, and no slate dust; the boy noticed the absence and could not ask what it meant. He told a pot \emph{you’ll do} and \emph{the shoulder’s thick}, told the wheel it did not care whose hands, only if they were steady, and moved the damper before Sella had finished telling him the fire was low, going in with the bent finger ahead of his hand. He did not say the back room was cold and did not look toward the basket or the bed. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed; the foundling went on being carried under the roof unwritten.

\textbf{Ch 7.} On Stone 23, after five mornings of clean bone-coloured slip, he came in from the back room with fine grey slate dust worked into the creases of his forearms past the bend of the little finger and said nothing about where he had been; the boy read the arranged face the way he had once read a resident who kept his eyes on a chart. He told the pot she would want a thinner slip, told the wheel it did not care whose hands, only if they were steady, and went to the damper before Sella had finished, the bent finger going in first. On Stone 25 the forearms were clean again and he kept dusty and clean as two entries; on Stone 29 the sweeping talk made him quieter and the yard straightened around it without an order. He knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and would not say so in front of a kiln-master, who would call it early and make something of it; the boy knows this about him as he knows the bent finger, and keeps both where questions can last for years. He did not say the back room was cold and did not look toward the bed; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed through the year’s last market.

\textbf{Ch 8.} Through the Five the wheel-shed gave him bone-coloured slip dried to old bone up both forearms and the bent little finger leading at the damper; he moved the damper before Sella had finished and did not say the back room was cold. No slate dust came after the Last Day and he never mentioned the back room; he did not look toward the bed or the basket. On the Last Day the grey in the corners was still where it lay and the baking went on around it, and he went quieter as the sweeping talk went around. On Ilmen 1 he worked the slip toward the thaw and the pits with the same forearms and the same silence, and the foundling went into the new year carried under the roof without a Vail name.

\textbf{Ch 9.} On Ilmen 4 he came in from the back room with fine grey slate dust worked into the creases of his forearms past the bend of the little finger and said nothing about where he had been; on the other mornings the forearms carried bone-coloured slip, and the boy kept the two states apart. He told a pot it would do, told the wheel it did not care whose hands, and went to the damper before Sella had finished, the bent finger going in ahead of his hand. He knew the full note of a Vail pot before it left the wheel and would not say so before a kiln-master. He agreed with nobody about the thaw and contradicted nobody, and his silence went around the yard as its own weather signal. He did not look toward the basket and did not say the back room was cold.

\textbf{Ch 10.} He comes in from the wheel-shed with bone-coloured slip dried to old bone up both forearms and no grey slate dust worked into the creases past the bend of his little finger on the days the boy watches; on Ilmen 11 the bent finger goes in ahead of his hand at the damper and he moves it before Sella has finished telling him the fire is low, so she shuts her mouth on the instruction and gives it to the pot. He tells a pot \emph{You’ll do} and tells the wheel it does not care whose hands are on it, only if they are steady, and does not say the back room is cold. He does not look toward the basket or the bed, has not been told about the woman in the brook and has not asked. Garl’s proverb still goes to the pot and his own unfinished sentence still goes nowhere; \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed through seven more days.

\textbf{Ch 11.} He came in from the wheel-shed on all three days with slip dried to the colour of old bone up both forearms and no grey worked past the bend of his little finger, the bent finger going in ahead of his hand at the damper each time, moved before Sella had finished telling him the fire was low. He told a pot \emph{You’ll do} and the wheel what it had been told a hundred times --- that it did not care whose hands were on it, only if they were steady --- and said nothing of the room off the shed, whose door kept its finger’s width of open. He did not say the back room was cold and did not look toward the bed or the basket. Garl’s salt-stiff coat kept a broader man’s shape on its peg, the hollow seat its twenty-year lean, and the clean dark line where the ridge had turned was not swept, because a line left where it is is still a line kept. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed as tightly as on the hour it was spoken.

\textbf{Ch 12.} On Day 50 he came in from the room off the shed with grey slate dust past the bent finger and said nothing, and Sella did not ask; the dust went on a tray of its own beside the clean slip of the other mornings. He told the pots and the wheel and not the basket, moved the damper ahead of her instruction with the bent finger leading, and did not say the back room was cold or look toward the bed. He knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and would not say so before a kiln-master. The promise of Corin’s name to the people who burn slates stayed where it has always stayed, ungiven and not withdrawn, and \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed.

\textbf{Ch 13.} He came in from the wheel-shed with slip dried to the colour of old bone up both forearms and no grey worked past the bend of his little finger. He spoke to the wheel before he spoke to anyone, told it what it had been told a hundred times --- it did not care whose hands were on it, only if they were steady --- and told a pot \emph{You’ll do} in a voice with no welcome in it and no unkindness either. He knew the full note of a Vail pot before it left the wheel and would not say so before a kiln-master, who would call it early and make something of it. Sella had not finished telling him the fire was low; his bent finger went in ahead of his hand at the damper and moved it, and the end of her sentence arrived at the pot instead of at him. He did not say the back room was cold and did not look toward the bed or the basket. The men who came into that room were not named and the broken birth-slates lay under the drying rack where the yard went around them and entered them into nothing; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed as tightly as a lid.

\textbf{Ch 14.} On Silt 4 the room off the wheel-shed kept its finger’s width of open all morning and Jorra came through with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bend of his little finger, not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel; two men had come in since first light and spoken low, and he gave the house no name for them. The broken birth-slates stayed under the lowest rack where the yard went around them and entered them into nothing, and the boy kept the dusty forearms and the clean ones on one tray as two states of one morning. Jorra spoke to the wheel before he spoke to anyone — it did not care whose hands, only if they were steady — told a pot it would do, and knew the full note of a Vail pot before it left the wheel without saying so before a kiln-master. When Sella had not finished telling him the fire was low, his bent finger went in ahead of his hand at the damper and moved it, so that the end of her sentence arrived at the pot and the household straightened around his silence. He did not say the back room was cold, did not look toward the bed or the basket; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed as tightly as a lid and the promise of the foundling’s name to the men who burn slates was ungiven and not withdrawn.

\textbf{Ch 15.} On Silt 14 he came through the finger’s-width-open door off the wheel-shed in the afternoon with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bend of his little finger, not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel; two men had come in since first light and spoken low and he named neither the men nor the room. The broken birth-slates stayed under the lowest rack where the yard went around them and entered them into nothing. He spoke to the wheel before he spoke to anyone --- it did not care whose hands, only if they were steady --- told a pot it would do, and knew the full note of a Vail pot before it left the wheel without saying so before a kiln-master from High Kiln. When Sella had not finished telling him the fire was low, his bent finger went in ahead of his hand at the damper and moved it, so the end of her instruction arrived at the pot and the household straightened around his silence. He did not say the back room was cold. On Silt 15 he came through again with bone-coloured slip dried to old bone up both forearms and no grey worked past the bend; the grey dust was the day before. He did not look toward the bed or into the basket. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed as tightly as a lid nobody had tried to lift in three years, and the promise of the foundling’s name to the men who burn slates was neither given nor withdrawn.

\textbf{Ch 16.} On Day 77, Silt 18, he comes through the finger’s-width-open wheel-shed door with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bend of his little finger, not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel; two men had come in since first light and spoken low in the back room and he gave the house no name for them. On Day 76 his forearms carried clean bone-coloured slip dried to old bone, and the boy kept the two states of one week on a single tray and asked neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate. The broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack, gone around by the yard and entered by nobody. He speaks to the wheel before he speaks to anyone --- \emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady} --- tells a pot \emph{You’ll do}, knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and will not say so before a kiln-master from High Kiln. When Sella has not finished telling him the fire is low, his bent finger goes in ahead of his hand at the damper and moves it, so the end of her instruction arrives at the pot and the household straightens around his silence the way cloth straightens when a weight is lifted. He does not say the back room is cold and does not look toward the bed or the basket. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed as tightly as a lid nobody has tried to lift in three years, and the promise of the foundling’s name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn.

\textbf{Ch 17.} On Silt 22 he comes through the finger’s-width-open door off the wheel-shed with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bend of his little finger, not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel; men came in since first light and spoke low and he gives the house no name for them. The broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack, gone around and entered by nobody. He speaks to the wheel before he speaks to anyone — it does not care whose hands, only if they are steady — tells a pot it will do, knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and will not say so before a kiln-master. When Sella has not finished telling him the fire is low, his bent finger goes in ahead of his hand at the damper and moves it, so the end of her instruction arrives at the pot and the household straightens around his silence the way cloth straightens when a weight is lifted. He does not say the back room is cold and does not look toward the bed or the basket. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed as tightly as a lid nobody has tried to lift in three years, and the promise of the foundling’s name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn.

\CRsheetheading{Arc So Far}
He enters at the wheel with his weight in the hollow his father wore and has spent three years failing to fill --- slip dried to the colour of old bone up both forearms, the left little finger bent from a splinter at eleven, a story about a fight he tells because a fight sounds more like him. In Chapter 2 he says one flat sentence about the foundling and is refused an answer, and the sentence is sealed by the boy’s arrival: a child lies under the roof and nobody has written him as Vail. He does not look at his mother while obeying her instantly, speaks to the pots before people, goes quiet when the levy is spoken of, and has given none of the men who come into the back room a word they can carry away. He is the most careful keeper of the Vail fire in four generations and is quietly helping the people who want to burn every slate in Sill, and has never once thought the two facts cannot live in the same man.

On Days 5 and 6 the back room comes into the house on his forearms as slate dust, grey and fine, worked into the creases past the bend of the little finger, and not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel. He tells the pots \emph{you’ll do}, shifts the damper before Sella has finished telling him and shifts it again at dusk, and says \emph{the back room’s cold} to nobody in particular --- not an answer and not a question, shaped so nobody can take it further. Sella does not take it further. The boy watches the dust and wants to know which slate was broken, and whether it was a birth-slate, and keeps the questions where questions can last for years.

On Days 7, 8 and 9 the wheel keeps the house’s time and the absence of dust is as much a fact as its presence was on Stone 12. He works in bone-coloured slip, speaks to the pots and the wheel and never to the basket, and moves the damper before Sella has finished: an obedience that is also a correction neither will name. He goes quieter when the levy is spoken around and quieter still at \emph{the house’s share}, and the yard straightens around him. The broken birth-slates under the drying rack and the men whose names are not spoken stay unshown; the back room is not entered in any roll the house shows, and its cold is not mentioned. He still wants the foundling outside the name and the hollow seat for himself, and has said neither.

On Days 10 through 14 the wheel keeps the house’s time and the absence of dust is the fact of the five days: slip the colour of old bone on both forearms, no grey worked into the creases. He speaks to the pots and the wheel and never to the basket, says \emph{you’ll do} to a pot and that the wheel does not care whose hands are on it, and shifts the damper before Sella has finished --- an obedience that is also a correction neither will name. He goes quieter when the levy and the debt are spoken around and quieter still at the reading at the Cross. He does not say the back room was cold, does not take up Sella’s silence, and does not look toward the bed where the foundling lies. The broken birth-slates under the drying rack and the men whose names are not spoken stay unshown; he still wants the boy outside the name Vail and the hollow seat for himself, and has said neither.

On Days 15 through 24 the wheel keeps the house’s time and the dust comes and goes. Five clean mornings make its absence a fact; on Stone 23 it returns, grey and fine in the creases past the little finger, and the boy sets the two states of the same forearms on separate places on a tray. Jorra speaks to the pot and the wheel, never to the basket, moves the damper before Sella has finished, and goes quieter as the Last Day sweeping talk goes around. He sets a pot down on the bench and does not turn to its interval, and the boy does not turn after him. On Stone 29 a sweeping that will leave the grey where it lies until it is burned and called dealt with makes the house straighter and him quieter; on Stone 30 he has moved the damper and not looked toward the bed. The full note is in a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel, which he will not say before a kiln-master, and the boy knows he knows. The broken birth-slates under the drying rack and the men in the back room stay unshown; the foundling goes into a new year carried under the roof without a Vail name.

On Days 25 through 30 the wheel keeps the house’s time and the back room is not once mentioned. The forearms carry bone-coloured slip dried to old bone and the bent little finger goes in ahead of the hand at the damper, which he moves before Sella has finished; no grey dust appears after the Last Day, and the boy, who once set the dust and the clean slip on separate places on a tray, has nothing new to file. He speaks to the pots and the wheel and never to the basket, does not look toward the bed, and goes quieter when the sweeping talk and the burned Ash come around. The full note is in a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and he will not say so before a kiln-master; \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed through the turn of the year, and the foundling goes into Y.H. 813 carried under the roof unwritten.

On Days 31 through 37 the wheel keeps the house’s time and the dust comes back from the room the house does not enter. On Ilmen 4 grey slate dust is worked into the creases past the bent little finger, not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel; the yard goes around the space under the drying rack where whole slate should have stood and enters it. He speaks to the pots and the wheel and never to the basket, moves the damper before Sella has finished, and knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel but will not say so before a kiln-master, who would call it early and make something of it. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed and the foundling goes on being carried under the roof unwritten.

On Days 38 through 44 the wheel keeps the house’s time and the back room is not once mentioned. At dusk on Ilmen 9 he came in from the wheel-shed with bone-coloured slip dried to old bone up both forearms and went to the damper before Sella had finished telling him the fire was low, the bent finger going in ahead of his hand, and neither he nor Tarn looked toward the bed where the boy lay; they had not been told about the woman in the brook and had not asked. On Ilmen 11 the forearms were clean of slate dust and the bent finger led again at the damper; he told a pot \emph{You’ll do}, told the wheel it did not care whose hands were on it, only if they were steady, said nothing about the back room and did not look toward the basket. He agreed with nobody about the thaw and contradicted nobody, and the yard straightened around his silence without an order. Through the Fish Blessing at the Weir he stayed in the wheel-shed, and \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed for all seven days.

On Days 45 through 47 the wheel keeps the house’s time and the back room is not once mentioned. The forearms carry bone-coloured slip dried to old bone and no slate dust past the bend of the little finger; the bent finger leads at the damper ahead of Sella’s sentence and the end of her instruction goes to the pot. He speaks to the pots and the wheel and never to the bed, tells a pot \emph{You’ll do}, and says nothing about the back room. He knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and would not say so before a kiln-master, and the boy keeps the knowing where questions can last for years. Garl’s proverbs go to the pot and the fire and never to the basket, and the clean dark line is not swept. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed through three more days and the foundling goes on being carried under the roof unwritten.

On Days 48 through 54 the wheel keeps the house’s time and the dust comes back from the room the house does not enter. On Day 50 he comes in from the back room with fine grey slate dust worked into the creases past the bend of his little finger and says nothing about where he has been; the men are not named and the broken birth-slates stay under the drying rack, gone around and entered by nobody. On the other mornings the forearms carry bone-coloured slip and the boy keeps the two states apart. He tells a pot it will do and the wheel it does not care whose hands, only if they are steady, and knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel but would not say so before a kiln-master, who would call it early and make something of it. The bent finger goes in ahead of his hand at the damper ahead of Sella’s instruction; he does not say the back room was cold and does not look toward the bed or the basket. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed through all seven days.

On Days 55 through 60 the wheel keeps the house’s time and the back room is not once mentioned. The forearms carry bone-coloured slip dried to old bone and no slate dust worked past the bend of the little finger, and the boy keeps the clean state apart from the dust days without being able to ask what either means. He speaks to the wheel and the pots and never to the basket or the bed, tells the wheel it does not care whose hands are on it, only if they are steady, and knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel but will not say so before a kiln-master, who would call it early and make something of it. His bent finger goes in ahead of his hand at the damper ahead of Sella’s instruction so that the end of her sentence arrives at the pot instead of at him; the yard straightens around his silence without an order. He does not say the back room was cold, the men in that room are not named, and the broken birth-slates stay under the drying rack, gone around and entered by nobody. The promise of Corin’s name to the people who burn slates stays where it has always stayed, ungiven and not withdrawn, and \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed through the turning of the month and the coming of Silt.

On Days 61 through 67 the wheel keeps the house’s time and the room the house does not enter puts its dust into the yard again. On Silt 4 Jorra comes through the finger’s-width-open door with grey slate dust past the bent little finger, not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel, says nothing about where he has been, and lets the men in that room stay unnamed. He keeps the two states of his forearms as one man’s two mornings and the boy keeps them on the same tray without asking which slate was broken or whether it was a birth-slate. Broken birth-slates stay buried under the lowest rack and the space above them is gone around as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it, entered by nobody. He speaks to the wheel and the pots and never to the basket or the bed, knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and would not say so before a kiln-master who would call it early and make something of it, and moves the damper with the bent finger leading ahead of Sella’s sentence so that the end of her instruction arrives at the pot. The yard straightens around his silence without an order. He does not say the back room is cold and does not look toward the bed; \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the foundling’s name stays ungiven and not withdrawn, while the hollow seat waits for his weight and the foundling goes on being carried under the roof unwritten.

On Days 68 through 74 the wheel keeps the house’s time through the flood and the room the house does not enter puts its dust into the yard on Silt 14. Jorra comes through the finger’s-width-open door with grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bend of the little finger, not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel, says nothing about the two men who came in since first light and gives them no name; the next afternoon he comes through with clean bone-coloured slip and no grey past the bend. The broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack and the space above them is gone around as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it, entered by nobody. He speaks to the wheel and the pots and never to the basket or the bed, knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and would not say so before a kiln-master who would call it early and make something of it, and moves the damper with the bent finger leading ahead of Sella’s unfinished instruction so that the end of her sentence arrives at the pot. The yard straightens around his silence without an order. He does not say the back room is cold and does not look toward the bed; \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the foundling’s name to the men who burn slates stays ungiven and not withdrawn, while the hollow seat waits for his weight and the foundling goes on being carried under the roof unwritten.

The bent finger leads at the damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence and the household straightens around his silence; the full note is in a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and he will not say so before a kiln-master. On Days 78 through 84 the wheel keeps the house’s time through a week in which nothing is settled, and the room the house does not enter puts its dust into the yard once more. On Silt 22 he comes through the finger’s-width-open door with grey slate dust past the bent little finger, not bone-coloured slip, and gives no name to the men who came in before light; the broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack and the yard goes around the space above them as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it. He keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray as two states of one man’s mornings and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate. He speaks to the wheel before anybody and to the pots and never to the basket, knows the full note before it leaves the wheel and will not say it before a kiln-master, and moves the damper with the bent finger leading ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence so that the household straightens around his silence. He does not say the back room is cold and does not look toward the bed; \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the name stays ungiven and not withdrawn, while the hollow seat waits for his weight and the foundling goes on being carried under the roof unwritten.

On Days 85 through 90 the wheel keeps the house’s time across the turning of Silt into Seed and the room the house does not enter puts its dust into the yard again. On Silt 27 he comes through the finger’s-width-open wheel-shed door with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bend of his little finger, not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel; men came in since first light and spoke low in the back room and he gives the house no name for them. The broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack, gone around by the yard as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it and entered by nobody. He keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray as two states of one man’s mornings and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate. He speaks to the wheel before anyone --- \emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady} --- tells a pot \emph{You’ll do}, and knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and will not say so before a kiln-master from High Kiln. When Sella has not finished telling him the fire is low, his bent finger goes into the damper ahead of her sentence and moves it, cold iron taking the cold out of his fingertip, so the end of her instruction arrives at the pot and the household straightens around his silence the way cloth straightens when a weight is lifted; he has not answered her with a word and has not looked at her, which is how he obeys her instantly. He reads the damper as any iron that stops a thing from running: the same bite that keeps a vessel whole can take the hand off a man, and no word in Grathic holds both mercies in one. On Seed 1 he is heard at the wheel and not seen, a low note and the word to a pot, with no figure coming out of the shed onto the yard. He does not say the back room is cold and does not look toward the bed or the basket. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed as tightly as a lid nobody has tried to lift in three years, and the promise of the foundling’s name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn while the hollow seat waits for his weight.
