The small bench knife lies at the very edge of its sill with six years standing in a thumb-mark his thumb has worn almost flat and the seventh nearly gone and never named, the one entry in this house the house cannot check; the unforged collector sentence lies beside it where he has kept it since the frozen ford, and he enters neither. Ash is worked into the creases of his knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and no scrubbing lifts it; the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holds what light there is and gives it back. He takes the broom only after it has been given its instruction, says \emph{Yes, house} to the woman who wants the thaw early and the man who wants it late, agrees so entirely that no argument can find a foot and keeps wanting the late because it puts off the paying, though the paying has stood in the ruts since the water went. His chest is tight and the breath from Seed 16 is still unspent, a small interval at the top of each reach where it should have gone in, a breath stopped against iron and never let through. On Reed 5 he puts his hand to the knife on its sill, moves it a hair’s breadth and sets it back where it can be checked, and tells the sill where it is; behind Jorra’s standing finger his bristles go on over the flagstones without the half-check, past the shallow bright patch the stones keep where the stroke stopped, and neither man names the other’s silence. On Reed 5 night, crouched to the kindling that smells of straw and tallow, he brings the sentence about the ear and the debt to the threshold of the word that would call the loan and stops there; the wood takes it as wood takes everything, without answer and without keeping, and the boy files the stopped sentence on the interval tray beside the half-beat, the unchecking stroke and his own held breath. Something must give at the end of the seventh year and has not given yet; the loan that can hear stays uncalled.

On Days 126 through 128 the seventh year is pressed further past its third tend and still held, and the thing that must give at its end has not given. Reed has come on and the reeds stand in the yard in armfuls judged by the arm that carries them; he takes the broom only after it has been given its instruction, says \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late and keeps wanting the late because it puts off the paying, though the paying has stood in the ruts since the water went. His knife lies at the very edge of its sill with six years in the worn thumb-mark and the seventh nearly gone and never named, the unforged collector sentence beside it, his chest tight with the breath from Seed 16 still unspent and a small interval at the top of each reach where it should have gone in. On Day 127, with the coals banked and the knife set back where it can be checked, he tells the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, and the sentence about the ear under this roof worth more than the debt that holds it comes a second time to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name; he draws the breath and does not spend it, says \emph{Yes, house} and goes on with the broom. The boy files the second stopping beside the first on the interval tray as two intervals and not two payments, and the loan stays uncalled. Under the wheel-shed Jorra’s bent finger leads at the damper ahead of an unfinished sentence and the dust comes out of the back room from men unnamed; Tarn’s stroke goes on over the flagstones without the half-check while the stones keep the shallow bright patch where it stopped, neither man naming the other’s silence. He never looks toward the bed or the basket and says nothing of the ear; Sella asks nothing within hearing. The silver clip-ring at his wrist holds what light there is and Ash stays worked into the creases of his knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line. Nothing is spent, called, named or joined, and the seventh year goes into the next days still held.

Three stoppings now stand on the interval tray and none of them is a payment. The seventh year is pressed past another tend of Reed, the knife back on its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh held where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it and the breath from Seed 16 still unspent. A thing stopped three times is not settled; the loan that can hear waits for the word that has not been said.

\textbf{Four stoppings now stand on the interval tray and none of them is a payment.} The seventh year is pressed past the middle tend of Reed, the knife back on its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh held where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it and the breath from Seed 16 still unspent. A thing stopped four times is not settled; a held word is a debt and a debt that can hear can be called, and the loan waits for the word that has not been said. The stroke goes on over the flagstones without the half-check and the two silences stay unjoined.

On Days 135 through 137 the seventh year presses nearer its end and is still held; the boy is carried past him at the half-pace and the day’s arithmetic goes on in loaves and weather. On Day 136 he takes the broom after its instruction, agrees with an early thaw and a late and wants the late because it puts off the paying; men unnamed go into the room off the shed and he does not ask about it, just as Jorra does not ask about the ear. With the coals banked and the knife set back where it can be checked he measures the kindling four, four and an empty fifth and tells it \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count.} Then the sentence about the ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes the fifth time to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name; he draws the breath and does not spend it, says \emph{Yes, house} and goes on with the broom over the bright patch without the half-check. The boy files the fifth stopping beside the first four on the interval tray as an object and not a rule, an interval and not a payment, and refuses to let five likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine. A thing stopped five times is a thing held, not settled; something must give at the end of the seventh year and has not given yet. The loan stays uncalled and the two silences stay unjoined.

On Days 138 through 140 the seventh year presses nearer its end than it has ever stood and is still held; the boy is carried past him at the half-pace and the yard’s arithmetic goes on in loaves and weather. On Day 139, with the coals banked and the small knife set back where it could be checked, he tells the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and then the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes a sixth time --- after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14 and 17 --- all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name; he draws the breath that should have gone in at the top of the reach and does not spend it, says \emph{Yes, house} to the fire and goes on with the broom. The boy files a sixth stopping on the interval tray beside five as an object and not a rule, an interval and not a payment, and refuses to let six likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and no payer has been named to any of the six. On Day 140 he takes the broom only after its instruction, says \emph{Yes, house} to the early thaw and the late and keeps the late because it puts off the paying; the knife lies at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it and the breath from Seed 16 unspent with a small interval at the top of each reach. Men unnamed go into the back room before first grey and he does not ask about them, just as Jorra does not ask about the ear; his stroke goes on over the shallow bright patch without the half-check and neither man names the other’s silence. A thing stopped six times is still a held thing, not a settled one; something must give at the end of the seventh year and has not given yet. The loan stays uncalled.

Through Reed 22–24 the seventh year presses from nearer its end to one tend from it and still does not give. The knife stays at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it and the breath from Seed 16 unspent; on Day 142 he reaches the word that would call the loan for the seventh time — after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 and 20 — and stops there with no figure and no name, spends the sentence on the kindling instead of the collector and says \emph{Yes, house} to the fire. The boy files the seventh stopping as an interval among six and refuses to let seven likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and no payer has been named to any of the seven. His stroke goes on past the shallow bright patch without even the half-check it had made once on Seed 22, and the equality under the roof holds at that place: Jorra’s finger leads at the damper, Tarn does not ask about the room and Jorra does not ask about the ear, and the two silences are not joined. No collector comes, the loan stays uncalled, and something must still give at the end of the seventh year and has not given here. Ash stays worked into the knuckle creases and his chest has been tight since the dark.

On Day 145 the seventh year stands one tend from its end and still does not give. The knife is at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it and the breath from Seed 16 unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach; Ash is worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line and the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holds what light there is. He takes the broom only after its instruction, says \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late and keeps the late because it puts off the paying, and his stroke goes on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch \textbf{without the half-check} while the stones keep the place where it stopped. He gives the men who went low into the back room before first grey no name and does not ask about the room, just as Jorra does not ask about the ear. At the going of the light, with the coals banked and the knife set back where it could be checked, he tells the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and brings the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it an \textbf{eighth} time — on Reed 26 after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20 and 23 — all the way to the word that would call the loan. There he stops with no figure and no name, draws the breath that should have gone in at the top of the reach and does not spend it, says \emph{Yes, house} to the fire and goes on with the broom. Sella, within hearing, gives the end of her instruction to the pot and asks nothing; neither man names the other’s silence. Eight stoppings now stand on the interval tray and none is a payment; eight likenesses must not be suffered to stand up and call themselves a doctrine, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and no payer has been named to any of the eight. The loan is uncalled, no collector comes, and something must still give at the end of the seventh year and has not given here.

On Days 147 through 149 the seventh year stands one tend from its end and has still not given. The small knife is at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it and the Seed 16 breath unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach; Ash is worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line and the pale clip-ring at the left wrist holds what light there is. He takes the broom only after it has been given its instruction, calls Sella \emph{house}, and his stroke goes on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check while the stones keep the place where it stopped. On Day 148, with the coals banked and the knife set back where it could be checked, he tells the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and brings the ear-sentence a ninth time to the word that would call the loan, stopping with no figure and no name; he draws the breath he does not spend, says \emph{Yes, house} to the fire and goes on with the broom. Sella, within hearing, ends her instruction at the pot and asks nothing; Jorra does not ask about the ear and he does not ask about the room, and the two silences stay unjoined. The loan that can hear is still uncalled and something must give at the end of the seventh year, but nothing gave here.

\textbf{Ch 37.} The firing month finds his seventh year still one tend from its end and held: six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check, the seventh at the lip of the sill where it cannot, the small knife at the very edge with the unforged collector sentence beside it, the Seed 16 breath unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach, his chest tight since the dark, Ash worked into his knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line and the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holding what light there is. He takes the broom only after it has been instructed and says \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late, wanting the late because it puts off the paying. On all three days his stroke goes on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without even the half-check; he does not turn along the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector, and no collector comes. The equality with the boy has stood a hundred and fifty-two days: his ear for a pot before a knuckle touches it, the boy’s turn toward the note before anybody makes it, two silences of one shape and a loan that can hear never called. At the going of the light on Day 152, with the coals banked, he tells the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}; the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes up as it had come up nine times before, but on this day it is \textbf{not} brought to the word that would call the loan --- it stops short of the threshold, no tenth stopping stands up to join the nine, and he draws the breath that should have gone in and does not spend it, says \emph{Yes, house} to the fire and goes back to the broom. Sella, within hearing, gives the end of her instruction to the pot and asks nothing; Jorra does not ask about the ear and he does not ask about the room. The nine stoppings stay nine objects with no payer named to any, a tenth before the seventh year is earned would be a debt invented to make the nine into a bill, and the absence of a tenth is a keeping and not a payment. No new scar or possession, no change of voice; the loan uncalled and something still to give at the end of the seventh year.

\textbf{Ch 38.} Tallow 4–10 finds his seventh year pressed nearer its end than it has ever stood and still held: six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check, the seventh at the very edge of the sill where it cannot, the small knife set back at the lip with Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it, the Seed 16 breath unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach, Ash worked into the knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring at the left wrist holding what light there is, his chest tight since the dark. He takes the broom only after it has been instructed and says \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late, going on all the while wanting the late because it puts off the paying. On Days 153 and 156 his stroke goes on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check while the stones keep the place where it stopped; he does not turn along the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector, and no collector comes. On Day 158 the seventh year is pressed still nearer and still held, and he takes the broom only after the instruction, \emph{Yes, house} to the early thaw and the late. The sentence about an ear worth more than the debt that holds it does not come up in these seven days: no tenth stopping stands up to join the nine, and the boy files no new interval, for a tenth before the seventh year is earned would be a debt invented to make the nine into a bill. Sella gives the end of her instruction to the pot and asks nothing; Jorra does not ask about the ear and he does not ask about the room, and the two silences stay unjoined. The nine stoppings remain nine objects with no payer named to any, the loan uncalled. No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

\textbf{Ch 39.} Days 160 and 161 are his days under the Vail roof (offstage on Day 162 at the Weir). The seventh year stands nearer its end than it has ever stood and is still held: six counted where the house can check, the seventh at the lip of the sill where it cannot, the small knife at the very edge with Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it, the Seed 16 breath unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line that no scrubbing lifts, the pale clip-ring at the left wrist holding what light there is, and his chest tight since the dark. He takes the broom only after it is instructed, says \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late and keeps wanting the late because it puts off the paying though the paying has stood in the ruts, and his stroke goes on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check and over the collector’s road without once turning along it; no collector comes. At the kindling he sets the knife back where it can be checked, tells the wood \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, brings the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it to his teeth and no further, with no figure and no name, and draws the breath he does not spend; the nine stoppings stay nine objects with no payer and no tenth before the seventh year is earned, and the loan that can hear stays uncalled (T036/T076, T061/T082). He does not ask about the room when Jorra comes through with grey dust, and he does not ask about the ear when Jorra’s bent finger waits at the damper until Sella has finished her sentence; the two silences stay unjoined and the fraction is not spoken by him (T035/T031/T062). In the clay pot in the loft he keeps the warm stone Sella gave him in the winter Garl died, two years gone and cold long since, which he cannot reconcile with the debt and has stopped trying to reconcile, which is not forgiving (T006 held). No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

Through Days 163–169 the seventh year stands nearer its end than it has ever stood and has still not given. He takes the broom only after it is instructed, says \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late while going on wanting the late because it puts off the paying, and sweeps over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check and over the collector’s road without turning along it; no collector comes. At the kindling on Day 165, with the coals banked and the small knife set back at the very edge of its sill, he tells the wood \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and brings the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it all the way to the word that would call the loan, stops there with no figure and no name, draws the breath he does not spend, says \emph{Yes, house} and goes back to the broom. The nine stoppings stay nine objects on the interval tray with no payer named to any and no tenth before the seventh year is earned; the Seed 16 breath stays unspent and the loan uncalled. Ash is worked into his knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring holds what light there is and his chest has been tight since the dark. The warm stone in the clay pot in the loft is cold and unreconciled with the debt, which is not the same as forgiving it.

\CRsheetheading{Chapter Log}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 1: Does not appear; the broom, the knife and the loft are held for Chapter 2.

\item Ch 2: Swept the kiln-house before anyone woke and stopped for two strokes at a pot’s flat note without turning his head or naming the sound. Put the small bench knife in his pocket, then took it out and put it back where it could be checked and said so unasked. Told Sella \emph{Six years. One to go. I’ve counted every one, and I won’t count the next.} Carried up from the Debt Loft with a broom on the third day, banked the coals, and said \emph{He’s a foundling. I’m a debt. Don’t put us in the same sentence, Sella.} when the boy was given a bed. Heard the second flat note of the three days from a pot set down on the bench and did not say what it was.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 4: Days 5 and 6. Swept before light on Stone 11 and again at dusk on Stone 12, with Ash in his knuckles and the pale ring at his left wrist. Took the small bench knife out and put it back where it could be checked, saying so unasked both times. His broom stopped for two strokes at the flat note of a pot through the shed wall and he did not turn his head, name the sound or say that it was a sound at all --- the second ear in the house, witnessed only by the reader. Said \emph{yes, house; I’ll sweep it; I swept it this morning; I’ll sweep it again} to the ground and kept his head down over the broom. Six of seven years counted, the seventh not counted. He said nothing about the note all day, and nobody asked him to.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 5: Days 7--9. On Stone 13 came up the yard with the small knife already back on its sill, checked it with his eyes only, and saw the boy turn his head toward a pot before Jorra set it down; his broom stopped half a stroke at the set-down that gave nothing and he said nothing about either. Counted six years of seven and held the seventh back, and stopped altogether for two breaths when Sella said he had done well, then swept again. At dusk put the knife back where it could be checked and announced it unasked, and kept his head down over the broom while Sella counted loaves and bits. Said nothing all three days about the note that did not come, and nobody asked him to.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 6: Days 10--14. On Stone 16 measured the kindling stack with his eyes, four, four and a space at the end, and said to the stack \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count.} On Stone 17 set the small knife on its sill and told the yard to check, stopped altogether for two breaths when Sella said \emph{you’ve done well} and said \emph{Yes, house} before going on; his broom checked half a stroke when a pot turned toward on the bench gave nothing. Scraped Ash from his knuckles with the knife, held the pale ring at his left wrist up to the light and put the knife back without announcing it this time. Named the kiln’s breath as the danger and said a man in Mud End who slept before a kiln with the damper shut was called a merciful death; said he would take the late thaw, a longer week before the paying. On Stone 18 said he had swept and would sweep again; on Stone 19 agreed a late thaw was a longer week before the paying and offered to check the ridge; on Stone 20, Account-day, told the yard again the knife was back on its sill and let his broom stop half a stroke at the place where no note had come. Six of seven years counted all five days, the seventh held back and never named.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 7: Days 15--24. On Stone 22 set the small bench knife on its sill, told the empty yard \emph{I took the small knife. I put it back. You can check}, and said to the kindling \emph{Six counted; the next I don’t count}; was sent for a collector for a neighbour two doors down and returned with a man whose cuff was soft from washing and fingertips the colour of skimmed milk gone off, who said \emph{the measure is taken and the account stands as entered} to a slate. On the way back his head turned a degree at a vessel’s flat note carried past the door and he did not name it or look at the basket. On Stone 23 swept around the place where a pot had given nothing and said \emph{I swept it this morning; I’ll sweep it again}; Jorra’s returned dust went unremarked by him. On Stone 25 and 26 his broom checked half a stroke at the place where a pot cracked in the yard with the flat knock and he said nothing about either; he wanted the late thaw because it put off the paying. On Stone 29 held the pale clip-ring at his left wrist to the light, said \emph{I can check the width, house. I’ve a thumb as good as any}, and took his eyes off the ridge. On Stone 30 the knife was back on its sill and announced once more, unasked. Six of the seven years counted every day, the seventh held back and never named; the ear kept silent and the loan uncalled.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 8: Days 25--30. Through the Five set the small bench knife on its sill and told the empty yard where it was, and said to the kindling that six were counted and the next he did not count; the seventh year was held back on every day. Scrubbed at the Ash in his knuckles that no scrubbing lifts, and kept the silence about the flat note all five days and about the boy’s ear as before. On the Long Night said in the dark that six years were counted and the next he did not, and set the knife where it could be checked; Garl’s coat held a broader man’s shape in the dark. Wanted the late thaw because a late thaw puts off the paying; on Ilmen 1 swept toward the thaw and the slip pits with the knife back on its sill and the seventh still held back, and did not touch the ridge or the mark.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 9: Days 31–37. On Ilmen 2 noticed the oiled paper had stopped lifting hard before he noticed the light, and swept toward the slip pits with Ash in his knuckles that no scrubbing lifted; six years of the seven counted, the seventh held back and not said to the paper or the boards or anybody. Agreed with the neighbour who wanted the thaw early and the one who wanted it late and kept wanting the late one, because a late thaw puts off the paying. On Ilmen 3 set the small bench knife on its sill and announced it to the empty yard --- \emph{I put it back. You can check} --- and scraped at the Ash in his knuckles. On Ilmen 5 swept near the bench and did not say what the pot gave or look toward the basket. On Ilmen 6 his head went a degree toward the pot that answered nearly full and he went back to his broom without naming the sound. On Ilmen 7 stood with the yard as the Singing Sill gave its low note early and the argument ended in weather, and said nothing about either. Through the seven days kept the silence about the flat note and about the boy’s ear, and carried the count into Ilmen 8 with the knife back on its sill and the seventh year held back.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 10: Days 38–44. Set the small bench knife on its sill before light on Ilmen 9 and again on Ilmen 11, told the empty yard \emph{It’s back. You can check}, counted six years of the seven and held the seventh back; Ash worked into the creases of his knuckles that no scrubbing lifted, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist catching the light. Swept around the place where the clay-heavy water had come up behind the drying racks and swept the road toward the Fishstairs over and over without looking along it, the road a man goes down to fetch a collector; no collector came for the woman in the brook and he did not go for one. Agreed with the early thaw and the late and kept wanting the late one because it puts off the paying. Said nothing about the sixth hearing the boy had heard out of a person on the bank, and did not look at the basket on the way back up the yard.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 11: Days 45–47. Put the small bench knife on its sill and told the empty yard \emph{It’s on the sill. You can check} on Days 45 and 46; on Day 47 put it back and told nobody, because the yard had already been told. Counted six years of the seven and held the seventh back every morning, Ash worked into the knuckles that no scrubbing lifts, the pale clip-ring catching the light. Swept the road down toward the Fishstairs over and over without once turning to look along it; no collector went down it and he did not go, and he did not say the omission had a name. Stopped altogether for two breaths when Sella said he had done well, then said \emph{Yes, house} and went on. Agreed with the early thaw and the late and kept wanting the late one because it puts off the paying. At the well on Day 47 went once over the collector’s road and again without turning. Said nothing about the boy’s ear or his own, and the loan that can hear stayed uncalled.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 12: Days 48–54. The small knife lay on its sill with six years counted and the seventh held back; Ash was worked into his knuckles that no scrubbing lifts and the pale clip-ring caught what light there was. His eye went a degree to the slack oiled paper at the window before the light did and he said nothing. A vessel gave its note past the yard door on Day 50 and another pot answered nearly full on Day 52 and his head did not turn at either; he did not call either a seventh hearing or name the sound. He agreed with the early thaw and the late and kept wanting the late one, because a late thaw puts off the paying; his broom went over the collector’s road on Days 50 and 53 without once turning along it and no collector came. He did not look toward the bed or the basket, and the loan that can hear stayed uncalled.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 13: Days 55--60. The small knife stayed on its sill with six years counted and the seventh held back, the one entry in the house the house cannot check; Ash worked into the creases of his knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist catching what light there was. At the well and in the yard he said \emph{Yes, house} to the neighbour who wanted the thaw early and to the one who wanted it late, and kept wanting the late one because a late thaw puts off the paying (T036). His broom went over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector, over and over, without once turning along it, and no collector went down it for the woman in the brook (T009, T090). On Ilmen 28 a vessel gave its note past the yard door and his head did not turn; he did not name the sound or supply the Grathic word for it and did not call it a seventh hearing (T061, T076). When Sella told him he had done well he stopped altogether for two breaths, then set the knife where it could be checked and went back to the broom. On Silt 1 he kept sweeping toward the thaw with the count unchanged; the loan that can hear stayed uncalled.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 14: Days 61–67. Set the small knife on its sill and told the empty yard \emph{It’s back. \item Ch 33: Day 139 and Day 140, Reed 20 and Reed 21, on stage at the hearth and kindling on the evening of Day 139 and at the flagstones and kindling on the morning of Day 140; offstage on Day 138. Took the broom only after it had been given its instruction and said \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late, keeping the late because it puts off the paying, though the paying had stood in the ruts since the water went. Knife at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it and the breath from Seed 16 unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach; Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line and the pale clip-ring at the left wrist holding what light there is. On the evening of Day 139, with coals banked and the knife set back where it could be checked, he told the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and brought the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it a \textbf{SIXTH} time --- after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14 and 17 --- to the word that would call the loan, no figure and no name; he drew the breath and did not spend it, said \emph{Yes, house} to the fire and went on with the broom. Sella, within hearing, gave the end of her instruction to the pot and asked nothing; Jorra did not ask about the ear and he did not ask about the room. On Day 140 three or four men went into the back room before first grey and he gave them no name; his stroke went on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch \textbf{without the half-check}. Loan uncalled, seventh year pressed nearer its end and still held, breath still unspent. No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 34: Day 142 and the evening of that day, Reed 23, on stage at the flagstones, the kindling and the hearth; offstage on Days 141 and 143. Took the broom only after it had been given its instruction and his stroke went on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch \textbf{without the half-check}, the stones keeping the place where it had stopped, while the three or four men who went low into the back room before first grey were given no name. His seventh year stood nearer its end than it had ever stood, the small knife at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it and the breath from Seed 16 unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach; Ash worked into the knuckle creases, the pale clip-ring at the left wrist holding what light there is and his chest tight since the dark. With the coals banked and the knife set back where it could be checked, he told the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and brought the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it a \textbf{SEVENTH} time — on Reed 23 after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 and 20 — all the way to the word that would call the loan, with no figure and no name; he drew the breath that should have gone in at the top of the reach and did not spend it, said \emph{Yes, house} to the fire and went on with the broom (T036/T076). Sella, within hearing, gave the end of her instruction to the pot and asked nothing; Jorra did not ask about the ear and he did not ask about the room. The boy filed the seventh stopping on the interval tray beside six as an interval and not a seventh payment and would not let seven likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine, for no payer had been named to any (T061/T082). Loan uncalled, no collector, seventh year one tend from its end and still held, the Seed 16 breath still unspent. No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 35: Day 145, Reed 26, on stage at the flagstones, the kindling and the hearth; offstage on Days 144 and 146. Took the broom only after it had been given its instruction and his stroke went on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch \textbf{without the half-check}, the stones keeping the place where it had stopped, while three or four men went low into the back room before first grey and he gave them no name. His seventh year stood one tend from its end and still held: the small knife at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it and the breath from Seed 16 unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach; Ash worked into the knuckle creases, the pale clip-ring at the left wrist holding what light there is, his chest tight since the dark. With the coals banked and the knife set back where it could be checked he told the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and brought the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it an \textbf{EIGHTH} time — on Reed 26 after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20 and 23 — all the way to the word that would call the loan, with no figure and no name; he drew the breath and did not spend it, said \emph{Yes, house} to the fire and went on with the broom (T036/T076). Sella, within hearing, gave the end of her instruction to the pot and asked nothing; Jorra did not ask about the ear and he did not ask about the room (T058/T079, T065/T095). The boy filed the eighth stopping on the interval tray beside seven as an interval and not an eighth payment and would not let eight likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine, for no payer had been named to any of the eight (T061/T082). Loan uncalled, no collector, seventh year one tend from its end and still held, the Seed 16 breath still unspent. No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 36: Days 148 and the night of 148, Reed 29, on stage at the flagstones, the kindling and the hearth under the Vail roof; offstage on Days 147 and 149. Took the broom only after it had been given its instruction, and his stroke went on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch \textbf{without the half-check}, the stones keeping the place where it had stopped, while men with collars high went low into the finger’s-width-open back room before first grey and he gave them no name. His seventh year stood one tend from its end and still held: the small knife at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it, the Seed 16 breath unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring at the left wrist holding what light there was, and his chest tight since the dark. With the coals banked and the knife set back where it could be checked, he told the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and brought the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it a \textbf{NINTH} time — on Reed 29 after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23 and 26 — all the way to the word that would call the loan, and stopped there with no figure and no name; he drew the breath that should have gone in at the top of the reach and did not spend it, said \emph{Yes, house} to the fire and went on with the broom without the half-check (T036/T076). Sella, within hearing, gave the end of her instruction to the pot and asked nothing; Jorra did not ask about the ear and he did not ask about the room, and the two silences stayed unjoined (T058/T079, T065/T095). The boy filed the ninth stopping on the interval tray beside eight as a ninth interval and not a ninth payment, and would not let nine likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine, for no payer had been named to any of the nine (T061/T082). The carried fire kept its four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and forty-eight days (T088). Loan uncalled, no collector, seventh year one tend from its end and still held, the Seed 16 breath still unspent. No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 37: Days 150 and 152, Tallow 1 and 3, on stage at the kindling, the hearth and the flagstones under the Vail roof (also in the yard on Day 150); offstage on Day 151. Took the broom only after it had been instructed and said \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late, wanting the late because it puts off the paying. His seventh year stood one tend from its end and still held, the knife at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house could check and the seventh where it could not, the unforged collector sentence beside it and the Seed 16 breath unspent; Ash was worked into his knuckle creases and the pale clip-ring held what light there is. His stroke went over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check on both days, and he did not turn along the collector road; no collector came. On Day 150 Jorra’s bent finger went into the damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence and he did not ask about the room while Jorra did not ask about the ear. On Day 152, with the coals banked and the knife at the edge of its sill, he told the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and the ear-sentence came up as on the nine earlier days but this time stopped SHORT of the threshold: no word that would call the loan, no figure, no name, no tenth stopping, the breath drawn and not spent, \emph{Yes, house} to the fire, back to the broom (T036/T076). The boy filed the absence of a tenth as a keeping, not a payment (T061/T082). Sella gave the end of her instruction to the pot and asked nothing. No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 38: Days 153, 154, 156, 158, on stage four of the seven days; offstage at the Weir on Day 155 and at the shelf on Day 157. Took the broom only after instruction and said \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late, wanting the late because it puts off the paying; his seventh year pressed nearer its end than it had ever stood and still held, six counted where the house can check and the seventh at the lip of the sill where it cannot, the small knife at the very edge with Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it, the Seed 16 breath unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach, Ash worked into the knuckles and the pale clip-ring at the left wrist holding what light there is (T036/T076). His stroke went on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check while the stones kept the place where it stopped, and he did not turn along the collector road; no collector came. On Day 154 Jorra’s bent finger led at the damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence and neither man named the other’s silence; on Day 158 the dust and the finger in the iron stood again while he took the broom only after instruction, the seventh year pressed nearer and still held. The ear-sentence did not come up in these seven days: no tenth stopping stood up to join the nine, the boy filed no new interval, the nine remained nine objects with no payer named to any, and the loan stayed uncalled (T061/T082). Sella gave the end of her instruction to the pot and asked nothing; Jorra did not ask about the ear and he did not ask about the room. No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 39: Days 160 and 161, Tallow 11 and 12, on stage at the hearth, the flagstones, the kindling and the yard; offstage on Day 162. Took the broom only after instruction and said \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late, wanting the late because it puts off the paying; seventh year nearer its end than ever and still held, six counted where the house can check and the seventh at the lip of the sill where it cannot, small knife at the very edge with Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it, Seed 16 breath unspent, chest tight since the dark, Ash in the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line and the pale clip-ring at the left wrist holding what light there is (T036/T076). Stroke over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check, and over the collector’s road without turning along it; no collector came. At the kindling told the wood \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, brought the ear-sentence to his teeth and no further with no figure and no name, drew the breath he did not spend, and left the loan uncalled with nine stoppings still nine and no tenth (T061/T082). When Jorra’s bent finger waited at the damper on Day 161 until Sella had finished her sentence he said nothing of the fraction, and neither man named the other’s silence. The warm stone Sella gave him in the winter Garl died is still in his clay pot in the loft, cold and unreconciled with the debt, and he has stopped trying, which is not forgiving (T006 held). No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 40: Days 163, 164, 165, 166 and 168, on stage under the Vail roof, at the kindling, the damper, the flagstones and in the yard; offstage on the Weir day and the Account-day. Took the broom only after it was instructed and said \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late, going on wanting the late because it puts off the paying (T036/T076). Seventh year nearer its end than it has ever stood and still held: six counted where the house can check and the seventh at the lip of the sill where it cannot, the small knife at the very edge with Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it, Seed 16 breath unspent, chest tight since the dark, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line and the pale clip-ring at the left wrist holding what light there is. Stroke over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check and over the collector’s road without turning along it; no collector came. On Day 164, when Sella’s instruction to the fire went low, Jorra’s bent finger went to the cold damper and waited for the sentence to finish; he took the broom and said nothing of the fraction (T062), and neither man named the other’s silence. On Day 165, with the coals banked and the knife at the edge of its sill, told the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and brought the ear-sentence all the way to the word that would call the loan, with no figure and no name; he stopped there, drew the breath he did not spend, said \emph{Yes, house} to the fire and went on with the broom. Nine stoppings remained nine objects with no payer named to any, no tenth stood up before the seventh year was earned, the loan stayed uncalled and no collector came (T036/T076, T061/T082). A kiln-hand’s sideways word about the man in Mud End taken quiet in his sleep was called merciful and made into no lesson. The warm stone Sella gave him in the winter Garl died still lies in the clay pot in the loft, cold and unreconciled with the debt, and he has stopped trying, which is not forgiving (T006 held). No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

\end{itemize}
}

\chapter*{The Atlas}
\markboth{The Atlas}{The Atlas}
\addcontentsline{toc}{chapter}{The Atlas}
\CRmap*{The Cross and the Fishstairs — Sill’s market and the steps below the north bridge}{build/atlas/cross-and-fishstairs.jpg}{The ground the boy is carried over on every Account-day, drawn at the scale of the market: the market square with its stalls, the reading block under the moot-post and its finger’s width of shade, the eight pigs on the weighing rail and the turnips left standing with figures beside them, the Court’s table at the Slate Row fringe; below the north bridge the Fishstairs counting four steps, four, and the out-of-line landing, the edge of the fish-trade in the bridge’s shadow, Rusk’s room, the hard sill and the Singing Sill under the water, the dotted line of the Breaking, and the south bridge on the way to Low Kiln. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 813, the reed month.}

\CRmap{Greybank, the Court’s gate}{build/atlas/greybank.jpg}{The Court’s granary town eighteen leagues downriver of Sill, drawn as its own surveyors would draw it: the Ilm and its quay, the factor’s house where the tally for Sill is kept, the Vhaleni Counting House with Veno Brine’s private drawer of dry documents, the Court’s granaries and banking hall, the winter ford, the burial grounds, and the ends of the Clay Road and the beginnings of the Salt and Hearth Roads. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap*{High Kiln — the glaze terrace above Low Kiln, Sill}{build/atlas/high-kiln.jpg}{The other half of Sill, drawn at the scale a potter walks: the terrace two hundred paces above the low yard with its barley strip, House Clay and the folded red cord and locked box, the Glaze Room where lead is mixed and tasted, the master potters’ houses and their breathing kilns, the broken terrace lip, the steep street climbing from the north bridge and the Cross, the Ilm with its four-foot sill and Singing Sill, and Low Kiln below drawn faint for neighbourhood only. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap*{Sill and the Lower Ilm — the country of the birth-town}{build/atlas/home-region.jpg}{The clay country about Sill, drawn out a few days’ walking: the Ilm from Nine Pots and the Ferr to Greybank, the weir, the Old Kiln, Cold Acre, Mud End and the Reedholt marsh. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap{Sill and the Two Kilns — the birth-town}{build/atlas/home-settlement.jpg}{A detailed plan of Sill on the Ilm, drawn to the ground a child can walk: the four-foot fall and the Singing Sill, the two bridges, the Fishstairs and the Cross, Slate Row, Low Kiln with the Clay Yard and the Vail kiln-house, High Kiln and the Glaze Room, the family houses, the smithy, the meal mill, the wells and fields, the Bone Orchard and the edge of the reedbeds. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap*{House Silt and the Birth Room — Low Kiln, Sill}{build/atlas/house-silt.jpg}{The house three doors down the Clay Yard from the Vail house, drawn at the scale at which a basket set just inside the door sees it: the front birth room with its bench by the door, hearth and slip pot, board-bed of grey wool with the hollow where the pale river stone lay, the round pewter tin above the bed with its pale fold and thumb-bright rub, the shelf’s chipped cup, the birth-slate and the six narrow pages turned face-down toward a floorboard, and the grey Ash ridge left where it lies along the skirting into the back room. There a neighbour scrubs at a board with lye water and a low song comes up through the floor. Around it, drawn faint: the Vail kiln-house, the smithy, the Drawing house, the drying racks, the slip pits, House Reed and the birth-flower shrine, the Slip Brook where Dessa Silt was taken, and the nineteen counted steps. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 813, the month of Tallow.}

\CRmap{Keld Keep and the First Seam}{build/atlas/keld.jpg}{The Warden’s fortress city against the Rim and the deep survey cut into the stone beneath it, drawn cold and mineral as the Keep’s own survey-clerks would draw it: the walled Keep with the Warden’s hall and the mine-reeve’s room; the Rim Road coming up from Sill and going on ten leagues to the Cold Pass and its survey post; the Listening Stones five leagues higher in the Rim; and below, the timbered shaft of the First Seam with its galleries, the Descent, the Duelling Floor cut into the stone with nine clamps to the floor and the tenth behind the board, the survey room holding the crossed-out entry of Y.H. 588 and its branching red mark, the Ninth Gallery with the tin lined with warm-stone, a seam-serpent’s passing entered only as a change in the numbers, and the hot-lead warning of the Sweating. Cartouche dated Y.H. 812, the Thin Year, with a compass, a league scale, a convention of signs and surveyor’s notes on the measure before the name, the Warden’s claim, the once-a-year reading of the paper, and the insistence that no map is honest past the last pass.}

\CRmap*{Slate Row — the Court’s quarter in Sill}{build/atlas/slate-row.jpg}{The Court’s quarter, a quarter league east of the Cross, drawn at walking scale: the Clay Road passing through the Row to Greybank, the steep street climbing to High Kiln, the Ilm and its reedbeds along the south edge. The Court’s room with its bench by the door, pot, draught felt at the ankles and a place in the figures where a line should stand; the assessor’s narrow house of Y.H. 776; the collector’s table with its slate and cold-iron tube; the barred Waiting Room where the Forty of Low Kiln were held in Y.H. 812; the Court’s table at the market fringe and the printed one in twelve. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 813, the month of Tallow.}

\CRmap*{The Clay Yard and the Vail House — Low Kiln, Sill}{build/atlas/the-clay-yard.jpg}{The close ground of Low Kiln drawn at the scale a clay child walks: the Clay Yard with its slip pits and ruts, the Vail kiln-house with its hearth, loaf shelf and bed, the wheel-shed with the Debt Loft and the finger’s-width-open back room, the drying racks with the space beneath the lowest, the row of houses to House Silt, the smithy, the well and the birth-flower shrine, the Slip Brook behind and the Ilm at the reedbeds. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap{The Hearthseat on the Keel}{build/atlas/the-hearthseat.jpg}{The Court’s city, built over the Hearth a hundred and fifty leagues south-east of Sill, drawn cool and clean as its own surveyors would file it: the Weighing Hall with the grating of cold iron over the never-out fire and the Hearth shown in cut beneath the floor; Slate Row with the College of Assessors and its second file; the Steward’s room, the sealed files, the bank where measures are pressed into newborn vessels, the rooms of fewer than twenty Kept, the back rooms, the printed notice, the Hearth Road from Greybank and the way out to the Nine Wells. Surveyed and filed in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap*{The Old Kiln and the Ash Throat — one league south of Sill}{build/atlas/the-old-kiln.jpg}{The collapsed kiln in the grey clay a league south of Sill, drawn as its surveyor would draw it: the fallen crown and its broken brickwork, the fire mouth on the south-east flank, the flue broken at the top, the concentric throat where the ash runs deeper than a man, the hollow in its wall from which a slate was carried north to Low Kiln, the grey banks that will not take a glaze, the surveyor’s stakes and his cord, the track from Sill and the marsh way to Reedholt. A slow coil copied from the back of a slate is inked into the margin and left unread. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap*{The Weir and the Eel Traps — one league upriver of Sill}{build/atlas/the-weir.jpg}{The eel weir on the Ilm a league upriver of Sill, drawn at the ground the trap-keepers walk: the V of stakes and its traps, the plank walk, Orra Weir’s hut and salting-racks, the hearth-maids’ blessing stone, the shoals and reeds, and the river road. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap*{Vhal and the Sallow coast}{build/atlas/vhal.jpg}{A salt-chart of the principal Vhaleni port and the five leagues of shore east of it, drawn in the tar-and-wet-rope manner of the Council’s own surveyors: the Quay with its piers, crane, moored salt boats and the pulled benches; the Council room that smells of tar and wet rope, the tide-tally house and the glass furnaces within the town; the Salt Pans outside it with their dippers at dawn and their drying salt-paper; the blue-green Glaze Cliffs stained by old lead workings, and the glass-sand pits behind them; the silt-mouthed Ilm entering from the west and the Salt Road coming up from Greybank by the coast pass. In the sea the Sallow draw runs seaward against the wind, with a brine-gull, a salt boat and a salt-thing by report, and a surveyor’s notes on boat-shares passing through mothers, contracts that rot in the damp, and children warned not to lick the cliffs. Cartouche dated Y.H. 812, the Thin Year, with compass, league scale and a convention of signs.}

\CRmap*{Sarn — the bowl between Hearth and Waste}{build/atlas/world.jpg}{The known world as its own surveyors would draw it: the Rim and the cold beyond, the Sallow Sea, the Keel and the Hearth, and the nations between. Surveyed in Y.H. 812.}

\chapter*{The Reckoning of Days}
\markboth{The Reckoning of Days}{The Reckoning of Days}
\addcontentsline{toc}{chapter}{The Reckoning of Days}
\begin{CRtimeline}
\CRday{Day 101}{Seed 12, Y.H. 813 (Secondday)  —  the Clay Yard, the loaf shelf in the Vail kiln-house and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  The boy was one hundred and one days old and nobody said so, while a neighbour at the loaf shelf reached past the bare board and named the old space at the row’s end as a thing that came in with the planting and the empty place at his ear as a child’s appetite in one breath without once seeing they were one absence, a witness planted for a far-off account (T097), and Sella Vail said the house where another would say I, instructed the pot, fire and broom but never the basket, and left both gaps unfigured, while Tarn swept the collector’s road over and over without once turning along it, his knife holding six counted years and a seventh nearly gone and still held as he told the kindling Six counted. The next I don’t count, and a woman moving a pot lifted it a hand’s breadth too high so something came up to the rim of a note and went back down without crossing it, giving nothing worth calling and adding no seventh, and at dusk Sella put him on his bed under the roof with the fold right and the thread frozen, the carried fire answering four, four and a gap under blind ash with its payer unnamed for a hundred and one days and the river’s note and the fire’s gap coming in two separate places as his hand went up an inch toward the water and came down, the count standing at one hundred and one unspent.}
\CRday{Day 102}{Seed 13, Y.H. 813 (Thirdday)  —  the Vail kiln-house bench, the Clay Yard, the yard well, the Vail wheel-shed and back room (not entered), and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  Tarn agreed the thaw early against late so wholly that no argument found a foot yet wanted the late because it puts off the paying, and swept the collector’s road without turning and did not turn at a vessel’s note, while Berr Clay came up the clay road with his office cord folded under his coat and glaze at one mouth-corner, wiped his thumb twice, read one in twelve, called the levy and took himself out of his sentence with There’ll be a slate at the watch and went toward High Kiln with his box locked and the true subtraction inside believing he had done a kindness, and a neighbour at the bucket-round only mentioned a counting room shut in the war with the damper closed and its men dead of the breath, a mention and not a telling with no third coming, while Jorra Vail came through with grey slate dust past his bent finger, named neither the men who spoke low in the back room nor the room, spoke to the wheel before anyone, put his bent finger into the damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence so the household straightened around his silence, and read the iron as the bite that holds a vessel whole and takes a hand off a man with no Grathic word for both, and at dusk the private file was unchanged and the fire kept four, four and a gap with its payer unnamed for a hundred and two days, the count standing at one hundred and two unspent.}
\CRday{Day 103}{Seed 14, Y.H. 813 (Fourthday)  —  the Fishstairs below the north bridge, House Silt three doors down, the Clay Yard, the loaf shelf and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  Sella set the basket at the end of the fish-trade shade where no slate lay and gave the instruction to the wool and the water and never to the basket, while Mira Silt worked the eels with silt dried pale in her neck’s hollow, answered whether the run would be thin with her own answer, moved eel-bones while deciding whether to lie and, when a buyer named a figure, put her thumb to the grey cord showing a second cord twisted twice beneath it that was never carried to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted, her board lying beside Orra Weir’s without touching, the steps coming back four, four and a landing out of line with the soft-cuffed clerk still set for an uncalled measure and no sixth sighting of the neat dark hand, and three doors down Alda Reed laid her birth-slates before turning to the fold, pressed the wool a breath too long, crossed two fingers at the birth-flower unknowing and covered the sign with a dead woman’s date, said Warm and breathing which was exact and not true, touched the tin in her bodice without opening it and left her sixth page face-down toward a floorboard with six unread and no seventh, the pewter tin above the empty bed kept shut, while below the sill a woman wound wool round a child’s dark foot and called it the cold while the yard called it weather, and at dusk the boy, one hundred and three days old and told by nobody, checked his file unchanged with six hearings and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid and the word forty unspoken, the shelf keeping two unnamed gaps and the fold one crust beside its empty place and no third in rooms that did not touch, and Sella set him on his bed under the roof with the fold right and the thread frozen, telling the fire it was the thaw as it answered four low pulls and a gap with its payer unnamed for a hundred and three days, the river’s note and the fire’s gap in two places as his hand went up an inch toward the water and came down, the count standing at one hundred and three unspent.}
\CRday{Day 104}{Seed 15, Y.H. 813 (Fifthday)  —  the worked strips east of Low Kiln in the barley fields, the Clay Yard, the loaf shelf in the Vail kiln-house and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  The hands the strips were said to want went into the worked brown ground at last, counted in glances and handfuls and never in a figure, as a woman let seed out of a fist and would not say what it held and a man with a barrow shaped the number of hands and thought better of it so the figure went from the strip to his teeth and back, while Berr Clay came down off the north road with his office cord folded, wiped his thumb twice, read one in twelve as the notice says, said a number goes into a slate not into a strip, took himself out of his own sentence and went off toward High Kiln with his box locked and the true subtraction inside, and Sella gave the bucket and the broom their instructions before anybody and never the basket, moved her lips along the loaf row and gave nobody a figure, went around every open slate and the space under the rack at a half-pace and said the house where another woman would have said I, and at the loaf shelf a neighbour reached past the bare board before looking at the boy and said the old place at the row’s end had come in with the planting and went with her pot without ever seeing the empty place at his ear, T097 advanced and not paid, and at dusk the boy, one hundred and four days old and told by nobody, set the direction carried for a month beside the number the yard would not give and kept them on two places, his hand going up an inch toward the worked strip and coming down, the count standing at one hundred and four unspent.}
\CRday{Day 105}{Seed 16, Y.H. 813 (Sixthday)  —  the Vail wheel-shed and its finger’s-width-open back room (not entered), the damper, the yard well, the collector’s road, the Clay Yard and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  Men came in before first grey and spoke low in the back room and Jorra Vail gave them no name and did not say the room was cold, coming through with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bent little finger, not bone-coloured slip, keeping dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, speaking to the wheel before anyone and telling a pot it would do, knowing its full note before it left the wheel and would not say so before a High Kiln kiln-master, and putting his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence so the household straightened around his silence the way cloth straightens when a weight is lifted, while the boy read the iron as the bite that holds a vessel whole and can take the hand off a man with no Grathic word for both mercies and filed it as an object joined to no kiln, and at the well Tarn took the broom only after Sella had given it its instruction, said Yes house to both an early and a late thaw while wanting the late because it puts off the paying, his chest tight since the dark with the breath he had decided not to spend, his knife on its sill with six years worn almost flat and the seventh nearly gone and still held, to the kindling Six counted. The next I don’t count, ash worked into his knuckle creases and the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holding the little light, his broom going over the collector’s road over and over without once turning along it and no collector coming, the held breath pressed to its edge without giving, as at dusk the file stood unchanged with six hearings and no seventh, one crust stiff in the fold, the new grey unswept and the two sounds in two places, the count at one hundred and five unspent.}
\CRday{Day 106}{Seed 17, Y.H. 813 (Seventhday)  —  the Fishstairs below the north bridge, House Silt three doors down, the Clay Yard, the Vail kiln-house loaf shelf and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  Sella set the basket at the end of the fish-trade shade where no slate lay and gave the instruction to the wool and the water and never to the basket, while Mira Silt worked the eels with slime dried on her sleeves and silt pale in her neck’s hollow, answered whether the run would be thin with her own answer, moved eel-bones while deciding and put her thumb under her apron to the grey cord when a buyer named a figure, showing the second cord twisted twice beneath it that was never carried to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted and the knot for the thin child upriver untouched, her board beside Orra Weir’s without touching and Orra watching without an answer, the steps coming back four four and a landing a hand’s breadth out of line that a whole market walked over without a fall and the soft-cuffed clerk still set at the landing with his slate for an uncalled measure and no sixth sighting of the neat dark hand, and three doors down Alda Reed laid her birth-slates before turning to the fold, pressed the wool a breath too long, crossed two fingers at the birth-flower’s red edge unknowing and covered the sign with a dead woman’s date, said Warm and breathing which was exact and not true, touched the tin in her bodice without opening it and left her sixth page face-down with six unread and no seventh, the mercy-lie curdled to fact, while under the roof the boy, one hundred and six days old and told by nobody, turned out his file and found it unchanged with six hearings and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, three intervals, the word forty unspoken with the double turn beside it, four low things with the river’s note a fifth, the two shut-room tellings joined to no kiln, the damper’s bite filed and the loan uncalled, the shelf keeping two unnamed gaps and the fold one crust beside its empty place and no third in rooms that did not touch, and Sella set him on his bed with the fold right and the thread frozen, told the fire it was the thaw as it answered four low pulls and a gap with its payer unnamed for a hundred and six days, the river’s note and the fire’s gap in two places as his hand went up an inch toward the water and came down, the count standing at one hundred and six unspent.}
\CRday{Day 107}{Seed 18, Y.H. 813 (Eighthday)  —  the wheel-shed kindling sill, the yard well, the collector’s road, the worked strips east of Low Kiln, House Silt three doors down, the loaf shelf under the Vail roof and the bed under the roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  Tarn’s small bench knife lay on its sill with six years worn almost flat by his thumb and the seventh nearly gone and still held, the one entry in this house the house cannot check, and to the kindling he said \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} while his chest stayed tight with a breath he had decided not to spend, his broom going over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector over and over without once turning along it and no collector coming, while the planting went on in the strips in glances and handfuls and never a figure; three doors down Alda Reed laid her birth-slates on the bench before turning to the fold, pressed the wool a breath too long, crossed two fingers at the birth-flower unknowing and covered the sign with a dead woman’s date, said \emph{Warm and breathing} which was exact and not true, left her sixth slate face-down with six pages unread and the tin in her bodice shut; at the loaf shelf a second neighbour named the old gap as a thing the planting brought in and went with her pot without seeing the empty place at his ear, two tellings of one absence kept on two places with no third and no finger laid across, T097 advanced and not paid; under the roof the boy, one hundred and seven days old and told by nobody, read the held breath as a breath held against a clamp, exact and worth nothing, and added one hundred and seven to a count nobody could check.}
\CRday{Day 108}{Seed 19, Y.H. 813 (Ninthday)  —  the Vail wheel-shed and its finger’s-width-open back room (not entered), the damper, the Clay Yard, the dawn market below the north bridge at the Fishstairs and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  Men came in before first grey and spoke low in the back room and Jorra Vail gave them no name, coming through with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bent little finger, not bone-coloured slip, speaking to the wheel before anyone (\emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady}), telling a pot it would do and putting his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence so the household straightened around his silence, while the boy read the iron as the bite that holds a vessel whole and takes the hand off a man with no Grathic word for both mercies and filed it as an object joined to no kiln; at the dawn market Mira Silt answered whether the run would be thin with her own answer (\emph{Thin? Who’s to say thin? It comes when it comes. Ask the river}), moved eel-bones while deciding and put her thumb to the grey cord when a figure was named, showing the second twisted twice beneath it with neither knot counted and her board beside Orra Weir’s without touching, while a foundling in cast-offs turned his head toward a pot a half-beat after the boy’s, after the knuckle and after the note, then stopped and rubbed the green sliver at his throat twice and could not say why, no loaf passing and no secret changing hands that a slate could read; the soft-cuffed clerk still sat for a measure nobody called with hand to slate before eyes to stalls and no sixth sighting of the neat dark hand, and at dusk the count stood at one hundred and eight unspent with the watcher’s turn laid beside the two shelf tellings and joined to neither.}
\CRday{Day 109}{Seed 20, Y.H. 813 (Tenthday, Account-day)  —  the Cross reading block and moot-post’s shade, the worked strips east of Low Kiln, the Court table at the Slate Row fringe, the Clay Yard and the bed under the Vail kiln-house roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  On Account-day eight pigs went over the wet reading block and a clerk at the Slate Row fringe wrote a figure down in a second hand, his hand going to the slate before his eyes to the rail, while Berr Clay came up with the red wool cord of his office folded under his coat and green glaze at one corner of his mouth, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, read \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says} twice low into the crowd leaning over the very ground the hands had gone into on Seed 15, said \emph{The levy is called. It is not called by me} and, to a man who brought a number up out of a fist, \emph{A number goes into a slate, not into a strip; if the house wants it again, there’ll be a slate at the watch}, taking himself out of his own sentence and going off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction inside believing he had done the district a kindness, so that the figure read was not the figure paid and a figure read from a slate at a date was entered everywhere while a figure let fall from a fist into a strip was entered nowhere; the bell went four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, the heard bell kept beside the told bell and no seventh hearing, word coming that the soft-cuffed clerk was still set at the Fishstairs for a measure nobody called and no sixth sighting, and under the roof at the going of the light the boy, one hundred and nine days old and told by nobody, turned out his file and found it unchanged with six hearings and no seventh, the word forty unspoken with the readable double turn beside it, the two tellings of the shut room joined to no kiln, the damper’s bite filed as an object and the loan that can hear still uncalled, one brown-edged crust stiff in the fold with its empty place unnamed and no third, the shelf’s two gaps in a room that did not touch it, the thread at his mouth frozen and unwiped, the fire answering four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been with its payer unnamed for a hundred and nine days, the river’s note through the finger’s-width-open door and the kiln’s breath through the floor in two places that did not meet, his hand going up an inch toward the water and coming down as the count stood at one hundred and nine, exact, unspent and spoken by nobody.}
\CRday{Day 110}{Seed 21, Y.H. 813 (Firstday)  —  the edge of the worked strips east of Low Kiln, the loaf shelf in the Vail kiln-house, the Clay Yard and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  The planting entered its last tend with the hands in the strips counted in glances and handfuls and never a figure, a man with a barrow shaping a number and thinking better of it, while Sella Vail carried the boy at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the bucket, broom, pot and fire their instructions before anybody and never the basket, and at the loaf shelf a neighbour reached past a bare board before her eyes found the child, paused over the palm’s breadth that came in on Seed 6, closed on the loaf beyond and went off saying in one breath that the old space at the row’s end came in with the planting and this was the price of a wet thing set down wrong, never seeing the two were one absence or the empty place at his ear, T097 advanced and not paid, Sella moving her lips along the row without a figure and leaving the widow’s mark untouched, and at the going of the light he turned out his file and found six hearings with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced, the word forty unspoken with its readable turn, four low things with the river’s note a fifth, the two shut-room tellings joined to no kiln, the damper’s bite filed as an object and the loan uncalled, one brown-edged crust stiff in the fold, the shelf’s two gaps in a room that did not touch it, the knife at the edge of its sill with the seventh still held, his hand going up an inch toward the water and coming down as the count stood at one hundred and ten, exact, unspent and spoken by nobody.}
\CRday{Day 111}{Seed 22, Y.H. 813 (Secondday)  —  the Vail wheel-shed and its finger’s-width-open back room (not entered), the damper, the yard well, the clay road toward High Kiln and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  Men came up before first grey and spoke low in the back room and Jorra Vail gave them no name, coming through with fine grey slate dust ground into both forearms past the bent finger, not bone-coloured slip, speaking to the wheel before anyone (\emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady}), telling a pot \emph{You’ll do} and putting that finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence so the household straightened around his silence, the iron taking the cold out of the fingertip and giving it back a little warmer, while Tarn took the broom only after it was instructed and his stroke checked half a beat behind Jorra’s standing finger before going on without a word or a turn of the head, the two silences standing in one room with no hand joining them and the loan uncalled, at the well Sella sending the woman with wet sleeves to ask the pot what a wet thing costs because \emph{the house has said it}, Berr Clay wiping his thumb twice on his apron, reading one in twelve and saying a number goes into a slate, not into a strip, then going off up the clay road with the box locked and the true subtraction inside believing he had done a kindness, a man putting his fist back in his sleeve so the figure arrived nowhere, Tarn saying \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late while wanting the late because it puts off the paying, his chest tight and his breath unspent, and at going of light the count standing at one hundred and eleven, exact and unspent.}
\CRday{Day 112}{Seed 23, Y.H. 813 (Thirdday)  —  the Fishstairs below the north bridge and the outer boards of the fish-trade shade, House Silt three doors down, the loaf shelf in the Vail kiln-house and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  Sella set the basket at the end of the shade where no slate lay, gave the instruction to the wool and the running water and never to the basket, and stood a half-pace from every open slate, while Mira Silt answered whether the run would be thin with her own answer (\emph{Thin? Who’s to say thin? It comes when it comes.
