then came the chapter’s one meaningful change: standing with her back to the basket and moving her lips along the row, she reached a finger BENEATH the front edge where the charcoal tally lies in clusters pressed hard or faded nearly into the grain, as on Days 151, 157 and 160, but this time \textbf{held the finger under the board for the length of one of the breaths she counted} --- the small intake at the top, the hold, the letting go --- before bringing it away, without looking, reading, copying or giving a word and without going back to the shelf when the light went, and the boy saw the held beat from the low angle and filed it on a place of its own as a change held and unspoken, not a reading of the charcoal, not a payment, with no payer named to it, keeping it from the Day 161 fraction at the damper and the older intervals at Stone 13, 17 and 25 so that no likeness stood up and called itself a rule, for a rule is an account that has found a payer and no payer stood to any of them (T100 carried and advanced, not paid; T061/T082); the shelf kept its two unnamed gaps, the old space at the row’s end and the palm’s breadth that came in on the night of Seed 6, the crust in the fold kept its empty place unnamed, the pan’s gone place kept its round absence on a tray of its own, the sixth green stayed a colour joined to no ear and the foundling a shape with no sale, and no third gap came and no fourth likeness was made a cause (T060/T086, T097); at the going of the light she set him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread frozen and unwiped, let her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed, told the fire it was the thaw, said The house will keep it, counted under her breath toward no opening, pushed coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and left the widow’s mark untouched, because a dusk is not an opening and the two rooms do not touch (T058/T079); in the small hours he turned out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel --- six hearings beside and never among with no seventh and none invented, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, the older intervals, nine stoppings as objects and not a rule with no payer and no tenth before the seventh year was earned, the damper’s double bite joined to no kiln, the Tallow 12 fraction and this evening’s held beat on separate places, the two shut-room tellings with no third and the told bell beside the heard bell --- and one hundred and sixty-six stood exact, complete and unspent while the charcoal waited under the shelf for a hand that was not his and a day that has not come.}
\CRday{Day 167}{Tallow 18, Y.H. 813 (Eighthday)  —  the clay road downriver to the Weir, the plank walk on posts, the flat blessing stone, the lower boards, the fish-trade shade below the sill, the out-of-line landing below the north bridge, the clay road home and the bed under the Vail kiln-house roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  The finished reeds had gone out of the day and lived only in the carrying arm, which kept the weight and not the cost, and a woman who asked what the last of the cutting would want was answered with the river and the weather so that no entry stood anywhere (T071/T072, T077); Sella set the basket at the edge of the work where no slate lay, gave the instruction to the wool and the running water and never to the basket and kept her half-pace; on the flat blessing stone the reed-cutter straightened his wool-grey cord gone dark with a working thumb, turned it once so the knots stood, tied one low with his teeth and a pull of the thumb, bit the end off and put it back inside his coat with the flat of the hand, telling the weir woman who asked what it held You can ask the cord and No more can the Court, without anger or a smile and with no knot counted or figure given, his hand to the cord before the trap and before the woman (T099 carried); Orra Weir, hands like old rope, pale eel scars uncovered, salt white at her wrists and the nasal Fen half-song flat in her voice where she was tired, pulled one knot down with a small flat knock --- the knock of a thing laid where it belonged, which the boy kept apart from the small flat knock of a vessel cracked all the way through --- and gave the woman who asked what the levy would take now the hands were out of the reeds the date The ninth of Ilmen. The collector’s boat came round the bend on the flood and had six oars. One man stood at the stern and never touched them, and to That isn’t the levy, It’s a date. The river takes what the Court doesn’t. You can shout at either one. I’ve tried, her forty-first double turn legible, tail tucked, left over right with the weight of a thumb, the word forty unspoken and her thumb’s return left undecided as a lie or the habit of counting (T024/T059/T025); Mira Silt, slime dried grey in long strokes on her sleeves and silt pale in the hollow of her neck, her head held a little right where the top of her left ear had been and her small smile like a door on the latch, answered a thin run with Thin? Who’s to say thin? It comes when it comes. Ask the river, flicked eel-bones while deciding whether to lie and told a buyer who named a figure Two marks the pair and two short. You’ve said it twice and I’ve counted it twice. There’s nothing in the sentence that wants an answer, her thumb under her apron to the grey cord longer than the figure required and the second twist twice beneath a shifted creel, neither knot counted and her board beside Orra’s and not touching, and she did not look into the basket; below the sill in the fish-trade shade a woman wound a child’s foot in three turns of wool and went on winding after the foot had gone dark, the cold to one woman and weather to the yard, and the boy read the extremity going before the core, a cold vessel that will not clot and the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody would perform, exact and worth nothing at two paces with no silt-leach, cause or cure named (T093/T094/T096); at the out-of-line landing the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set for a measure nobody called, his cuff grey from washing and grey again by midday, his slate turned inward and his hand to it before his eyes to the stalls, the market selling over him as water over a stone that lies where a stone lies and a girl with a creel taking the landing sideways without a fall or help (T090/T080); at the going of the light Sella carried him home up the clay road, woodsmoke before her and river wind behind, going wide around the pan’s gone place, the bare dark trough and the space beneath the lowest rack without explaining any of the turns, and under the roof set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread frozen, let her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed, told the fire it was the thaw, said The house will keep it, counted under her breath toward no opening, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and left the widow’s mark untouched; in the small hours the file was exact and worthless with the Day 161 fraction and the held beat beneath the shelf on separate places, and one hundred and sixty-seven stood exact, complete and unspent while the fire missed its fifth with its payer unnamed for a hundred and sixty-seven days.}
\CRday{Day 168}{Tallow 19, Y.H. 813 (Ninthday), the eve of the reading  —  the Clay Yard, the yard well, the drying racks and the edge of the worked strips, the edge of the Cross with the reading block under the moot-post, the flagstones, the hearth, the loaf shelf and the bed under the Vail kiln-house roof, the clay road home, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  The eve of the reading drew the district’s arithmetic together without making it agree: a number came up out of a fist at the well and went back into a sleeve, a row of loaves gave up its count to a woman’s lips and nobody’s mouth, a grey cord a league downriver kept its knots where no Court thumb would spell them, the carried fire under this roof answered four low pulls and kept the silence where the fifth should have been and the river kept a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings, all of it exact and none of it entered (T077, T071/T072, T088), and the boy lay in the basket and let the figures stand where they stood because a likeness in a row will call itself an account if no hand holds it apart and an account once it stands wants a name and a payer; Sella gave the instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot and the broom before anybody and never to the basket, said the house and kept her half-pace from every open slate even though there was no slate open in the yard, and the women went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the broken birth-slates beneath the lowest rack and the field’s empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried); at the well a woman moved her lips over a row of loaves and gave nobody a figure, a buyer brought a number up out of his fist, looked at it and put it back in his sleeve so that it arrived nowhere, a neighbour with a wet pot was sent to the pot with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it, and a kiln-hand raking a kiln mouth spoke sideways of a man in Mud End taken quiet in his sleep and called it merciful, and nobody made a lesson of it, put a figure to the quietness or entered a cause across the saying; at the edge of the Cross the square stood quiet with nobody leaning over the reading block, the pot board keeping the small round of dust where a cup had once stood, and a woman crossing with a pot said only that there would be a slate at the watch if a house wanted its figure again and went on with her pot; under the roof Tarn’s seventh year stood nearer its end than it had ever stood and had still not given, six counted where the house could check and the seventh at the lip of the sill where it could not, the knife at the very edge with Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it, the Seed 16 breath unspent at the top of each reach, his stroke going over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without even the half-check and over the collector road without turning, no collector coming, nine stoppings objects and not a rule with no payer named to any and no tenth before the seventh year was earned, the ear-sentence coming to his teeth and no further and the loan uncalled (T036/T076, T061/T082); Jorra came through with dust ground small as meal on both forearms, spoke to the wheel before anyone and told a pot You’ll do, and when Sella’s instruction came low put his bent finger into the cold iron of the damper and left it standing while her sentence arrived at the pot, not asking about the ear and not looking toward the basket; the boy set the Tallow 12 fraction at the damper and the held beat beneath the loaf shelf on two places of their own and would not let them make a pair, held two waiting hands apart as a surgeon holds two instruments apart on a towel, and kept the crust’s empty place, the shelf’s two gaps, the pan’s gone place, the field’s empty place, the sixth green as a colour and the foundling as a shape on separate trays with no third gap and no fourth likeness made a cause (T062, T100, T060/T086, T097); at the going of the light she carried him home up the clay road, going wide around the pan’s gone place, the bare dark trough and the rack space without explaining the turns, set him on his bed under the roof, put the fold right, left the thread frozen, let her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed, told the fire it was the thaw and The house will keep it, counted under her breath toward no opening, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and left the widow’s mark untouched, and in the small hours one hundred and sixty-eight stood exact, complete and unspent, spoken by nobody under any roof, the day that would bring the slate not named among the counts and the charcoal waiting under the shelf for a hand that was not his and a day that has not come.}
\CRday{Day 169}{Tallow 20, Y.H. 813 (Tenthday, the second Account-day and market-day of Tallow)  —  the Cross, the reading block under the moot-post, the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade, the pot board and market stalls, the clay road, the out-of-line landing below the north bridge and the bed under the Vail kiln-house roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  The second Account-day and market-day came up over the Cross grey and close with river wind under the eaves and hot clay coming down on the same breath from High Kiln, eight pigs going over the board before the light was properly in the boards and potters setting bowls on the pot board, and the boy, one hundred and sixty-nine days old and five months and nineteen days and told by nobody, lay in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade with cold iron at his cheek while the crowd leaned over the reading block above him (T071/T072); Berr Clay came up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one corner of his mouth, his hands large and clean, wiped his thumb twice on his apron before touching nothing, once for the slate and once for the figure that would be on it, held a narrow slate unopened to his forearm with the writing to his sleeve, passed a finger over the figure and let his eyes rest on it a breath longer than the writing required, and read One in twelve, as the notice says low into the crowd, saying The levy is called. It is not called by me and to the man with the number in his fist A number goes into a slate, not into a bundle and if your house wants it again there’ll be a slate at the watch --- your house, never I --- taking himself out of his own sentence as a surgeon takes a hand out of a field before the dressing goes on and going back to the pigs by the bell (T015/T041/T047, T077); the Sill assessor wrote the pigs’ figures down with hand to slate before eyes to the rail and then to his mouth, a buyer brought a number up out of his coat toward the weighing board, looked at it and put it back in his sleeve so that it arrived nowhere, and the printed figure stood unchallenged while the true subtraction went back up the clay road in the locked box, the figure read still not the figure paid, the two records kept in two places and not made to agree (T077); the bell went four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, the heard bell kept beside the told and its missing fifth not laid across the kiln’s missing pull or the boards’ knot (T078); Hessa Rale came through going up the clay road with Berr’s narrow slate held edge-on to her forearm and the writing to her sleeve, her hand to it before her eyes went to the crowd, the small flat correction of the strap and the turn of the wrist bringing the edge round, her coat shortened at the skirt for the road’s mud with the dried pale scurf unbrushed, two straps settled and the thumb along the grain with nothing pressing where the writing was, and to the woman who asked what she carried said I don’t read it. I carry it. There’s a difference, and the road doesn’t care which and to the next question Cross to Greybank. Reading goes up before noon. I’ve got a road to walk, answering the question that had been put and not the one behind it, without rudeness or apology; no figure came off the slate, and the boy filed the order of her reaching as the eighth such hand in the district on a place of its own, joined to none of Marra’s pause, the neat dark hand, the Court clerk, the soft-cuffed clerk, the soft hands at Slate Row, Berr’s twice-wiped thumb, the finger beneath the loaf shelf, the reed-cutter’s cord or Orra’s knot-string, for two records going inward are two records going inward and a shape is not a cause (T080 advanced and not paid); below the north bridge the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set for a measure nobody called, cuff grey from washing and grey again by midday, slate turned inward, hand to it before eyes to stalls, nobody taking him off and the market selling over him as water over a stone that lies where a stone lies, a girl with a creel taking the out-of-line landing sideways, catching the rail and going on selling without once looking at her feet and nobody making a fall of it (T090); at the going of the light Sella carried him home up the clay road, woodsmoke before her and river wind behind, set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay, kept her half-pace from every open slate, gave the wool and the river wind their instructions and never the basket, said nothing of what had been read over him, went wide around the pan’s gone place, the trough at the well and the space beneath the lowest rack, and under the roof set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread frozen and unwiped, let her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed, told the fire it was the thaw, said The house will keep it, counted under her breath toward no opening, pushed coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and left the widow’s mark untouched, because a dusk is not an opening and the two rooms do not touch (T058/T079); in the small hours the file was exact and worthless --- six hearings beside and never among with no seventh and none invented, three near-full answers advanced and not paid with the wheel-keeper’s knowing among them, the older intervals, nine stoppings as objects and not a rule with no payer and no tenth before the seventh year was earned, the damper’s double bite joined to no kiln, the Tallow 12 fraction and the Day 166 held beat beneath the shelf on separate places, the two shut-room tellings with no third and the told bell beside the heard bell --- the crust’s empty place, the shelf’s two gaps, the pan’s gone place, the field’s empty place, the sixth green as a colour and the foundling as a shape staying on their own trays with no third gap and no fourth likeness made a cause, three counts in three places not becoming one, and one hundred and sixty-nine standing exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool as his hand went up an inch toward the note of water over water through the finger’s-width door and came down against the fold, the fire missing its fifth under the floor with its payer unnamed for a hundred and sixty-nine days and the charcoal waiting under the shelf for a hand that was not his and a day that has not come.}
